body.text: Gaṇakārikā, 1
body.translated_text: <s>Gaṇakārikā</s> (Verses on the Categories), 1

children.text: pañcakās tv aṣṭa vijñeyā gaṇaś caikas trikātmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The groups of five are to be known as eight, and there is one <s>gaṇa</s> (category) whose nature is threefold.

children.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>
children.translated_text: [<s>Gaṇakārikāṭīkā</s> (Commentary on the Gaṇakārikā)]

children.text: * pañcapañcasaṃkhyāvacchinnāḥ samudāyāḥ pañcakā lābhādayas teṣāṃ nyūnādhikavyavacchedena aṣṭa iti saṃkhyām āha // GkT_1.1ab:1
children.translated_text: The aggregates delimited by the number five-times-five are the 'groups of five,' beginning with <s>lābha</s> (attainments) and so forth; he states the number 'eight' by way of distinguishing them as neither more nor less.

body.text: * tuśabdaḥ saṃkṣepavistāraparijñānayoḥ tulyaphalatvam avadhārayati śiṣyajijñāsānurodhena bhāṣyārambho 'py arthavān iti // GkT_1.1ab:2
body.translated_text: The word 'tu' (but/indeed) establishes that the fruit of knowing them in summary and in detail is equal; thus the commencement of the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) is also meaningful, in accordance with the curiosity of the student.

body.text: * vijñeyā viśeṣeṇa jñātavyāḥ punaḥ punar abhyāsena dṛḍhīkartavyā yena sarvadā śāstrārthe cittasthe kṛte sati granthavismaraṇe 'pi brahmodyadoṣo na bhavet // GkT_1.1ab:3
body.translated_text: 'To be known' means they should be known with special attention, to be made firm through repeated practice, so that when the mind is always established in the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), even if one forgets the text itself, the fault of failing in a theological debate would not arise.

body.text: * anuṣṭhānāśaktasyānyathā hi surāpānasamaṃ pātakaṃ syād iti // GkT_1.1ab:4
body.translated_text: For one who is incapable of practice, otherwise it would be a sin equal to drinking liquor.

body.text: * gaṇaśabdaḥ samuccayavācī // GkT_1.1ab:5
body.translated_text: The word <s>gaṇa</s> denotes an aggregate.

body.text: * caśabdaḥ samuccayena kevalam aṣṭa pañcakā vijñeyā gaṇaś caikas trikātmako vijñeya iti // GkT_1.1ab:6
body.translated_text: The word 'ca' (and) indicates that by aggregation, only eight groups of five are to be known, and one <s>gaṇa</s> whose nature is threefold is to be known.

body.text: * eka ity anantaroktāṣṭasaṃkhyāśaṅkānirākaraṇārtham // GkT_1.1ab:7
body.translated_text: 'One' is said for the purpose of removing the doubt that the number might be eight, as stated just before.

body.text: * trisaṃkhyāvacchinnaḥ samudāyaḥ trikaḥ // GkT_1.1ab:8
body.translated_text: An aggregate delimited by the number three is a 'triad.'

body.text: * sa eva ātmā svabhāvo yasya bhaikṣādivṛttigaṇasya sa tathoktaḥ vṛttyantaraniṣedhārtham // GkT_1.1ab:9
body.translated_text: That which is its essential nature — namely, of the <s>gaṇa</s> (category) of <s>vṛtti</s> (livelihood) beginning with begging and so forth — is called thus, for the purpose of excluding other kinds of livelihood.

body.text: * evam ete nava gaṇā jñeyatvonoddiṣṭāḥ // GkT_1.1ab:10
body.translated_text: Thus these nine <s>gaṇas</s> (categories) have been indicated as things to be known.

body.text: * yas tān samyag avadhārayati so 'vaśyaṃ duḥkhāntaṃ yāsyaty anyeṣāṃ cānugrahakaraṇasamartho bhavatīti // GkT_1.1ab:11
body.translated_text: One who correctly ascertains them will assuredly reach the end of suffering, and will become capable of bestowing grace upon others.

body.text: * kutaḥ punar etan niścīyata iti // GkT_1.1ab:12
body.translated_text: But how is this ascertained?

body.text: * niścīyate yasmāt sarvair eva paramayogibhiḥ vettā navagaṇasyāsya saṃskartā gurur ucyate // GkT_1.1ab:13
body.translated_text: It is ascertained because by all the supreme <s>yogins</s> it is said: 'The knower of these nine <s>gaṇas</s> (categories) is called the consecrator, the <s>guru</s> (teacher).'

body.text: * vida jñāne // GkT_1.1ab:14
body.translated_text: 'Vid' means 'to know.'

body.text: * tasya vediteti prāpte chandobhaṅgaparihārārthaṃ chāndasaḥ prayogo vettā iti kṛtaḥ // GkT_1.1ab:15
body.translated_text: When the expected form would be 'vedita,' the Vedic usage 'vettā' is employed to avoid breaking the meter.

body.text: * athavā vicāraṇe tasya vetteti bhavati // GkT_1.1ab:16
body.translated_text: Alternatively, in the sense of 'deliberation,' the form 'vettā' is obtained.

body.text: * vettā vicārayitā // GkT_1.1ab:17
body.translated_text: 'Vettā' means 'one who deliberates.'

body.text: * navagaṇānām iti bahuvacane prāpte chandobhaṅgaparihārārthaṃ tatparijñānasya bhinnaphalatvajñāpanārthaṃ vā navagaṇasya ity uktam // GkT_1.1ab:18
body.translated_text: When the expected form would be the plural 'navagaṇānām' (of the nine categories), the singular 'navagaṇasya' is used to avoid breaking the meter, or to indicate that the complete knowledge of them yields distinct fruits.

body.text: * nandimahākālādiṣv api gaṇaśabdo dṛṣṭaḥ tadāśaṅkānirākaraṇārtham asyety uktam // GkT_1.1ab:19
body.translated_text: The word <s>gaṇa</s> is also seen applied to <s>Nandi</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and others; to remove that possible confusion, the word 'asya' (of this) is used.

body.text: * asya anantaroddiṣṭasya lābhādikasyety arthaḥ // GkT_1.1ab:20
body.translated_text: 'Asya' (of this) means: of that which has just been indicated, namely the <s>lābha</s> (attainments) and so forth — this is the meaning.

body.text: * suparīkṣitaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dīkṣāviśeṣeṇa pañcārthajñānaviśeṣeṇa ca śiṣyaṃ saṃskurvan saṃskartā ity ucyate // GkT_1.1ab:21
body.translated_text: One who consecrates a well-examined <s>brāhmaṇa</s> as a disciple through a special <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and through special knowledge of the <s>pañcārtha</s> (five categories) is called the 'consecrator.'

body.text: * sa ca tajjñair mukhyata eva gurur ucyate // GkT_1.1ab:22
body.translated_text: And he is called <s>guru</s> (teacher) in the primary sense by those who know this tradition.

body.text: * gurur ācāryaḥ śraddhāvatām āśramiṇāṃ darśanasambhāṣaṇādibhir api pāpaghnaḥ puṇyātiśayakārī cety arthaḥ // GkT_1.1ab:23
body.translated_text: <s>Guru</s> means <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor) — the meaning is that for the faithful <s>āśramins</s> (those in the stages of life), he destroys sin and produces an abundance of merit even through seeing, conversation, and the like.

body.text: * athavā anyathā kārikāsambandhaḥ pradarśyate // GkT_1.1ab:24
body.translated_text: Alternatively, another connection of the <s>kārikā</s> (verse) is shown.

body.text: * dvividhaḥ khalv atra brāhmaṇo 'pavargagantā śrūyate sādhaka ācāryaś ceti // GkT_1.1ab:25
body.translated_text: Indeed, in this system, two kinds of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who attain liberation are spoken of: the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) and the <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor).

body.text: * tatreha darśane yaḥ sādhakaḥ sann apavargaṃ gantum icchati // GkT_1.1ab:26
body.translated_text: Here, in this system, one who, being a <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner), wishes to attain <s>apavarga</s> (liberation),

body.text: * śāstraṃ śrutvācāryopadeśamātrād vā vidhyādisvarūpaṃ jñātvā vidhiyogānuṣṭhānam atyantābhiyogena kartavyam // GkT_1.1ab:27
body.translated_text: having heard the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), or having learned the nature of the injunctions and so forth merely from the instruction of the <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor), must practice the observance of the injunctions with utmost dedication.

body.text: * yas tv ācāryaḥ sann apavargam gantum icchati tena kiṃ kartavyam iti āha // GkT_1.1ab:28
body.translated_text: But one who, being an <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor), wishes to attain <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) — what must he do? To this he says:

body.text: * pañcakās tv aṣṭa vijñeyā gaṇaś caikas trikātmakaḥ iti // GkT_1.1ab:29
body.translated_text: 'The groups of five are to be known as eight, and there is one <s>gaṇa</s> (category) whose nature is threefold.'

body.text: * tuśabdaḥ samastasūtrasūtrāvayavānām upodghātādiniścayadvāreṇa navagaṇā vijñeyās tān vijñāya śiṣyāṇāṃ saṃśayād yajñānaṃ nirvartayatā saṃskāraḥ kartavya ity evaṃbhūtaṃ viśeṣaṃ sūcayati // GkT_1.1ab:30
body.translated_text: The word 'tu' indicates a distinction of this nature: by ascertaining the nine <s>gaṇas</s> through the method of determining the preliminaries and so forth of the entire <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism) and its parts, having known them, one must perform the <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration) by dispelling the doubt and wrong knowledge of the disciples.

body.text: * śeṣas tv avayavārthaḥ pūrvavat // GkT_1.1ab:31
body.translated_text: The remaining meaning of the words is as before.

body.text: * kathaṃ punar etat gamyate // GkT_1.1ab:32
body.translated_text: But how is this understood?

body.text: * duḥkhanimittam ācāryatvam ātmana icchatā navagaṇā viśeṣato jñātavyā iti gamyate // GkT_1.1ab:33
body.translated_text: It is understood that one who desires the status of <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor) as the cause of ending suffering must know the nine <s>gaṇas</s> (categories) with special attention.

body.text: * yasmāt // GkT_1.1ab:34]
body.translated_text: Because —

body.text: vettā navagaṇasyāsya saṃskartā gurur ucyate // Gk_1.1
body.translated_text: The knower of these nine <s>gaṇas</s> (categories) is called the consecrator, the <s>guru</s> (teacher).

body.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: * evaṃ cānuṣṭhānābhiniveśāsamartho 'pi yadi śraddhānvito bhūtveṣad api samayamātraṃ pālayan jñānābhyāsaṃ na muñcati tadāpavargagantā bhavaty ācārya iti cocyate // GkT_1.1cd:1
children.translated_text: And thus, even one who is incapable of dedication to practice, if he becomes endowed with faith, observes even just the basic conventions, and does not abandon the practice of knowledge, then he attains <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) and is called an <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor).

children.text: * yas tv āgamārthajñānamātreṇa tuṣṭaḥ san śraddhādivirahitaḥ śraddhādimātrayukto vā lābhādijñānavikalaḥ sa khalv ācāryābhāsa eva nāpavargaganteti // GkT_1.1cd:2
children.translated_text: But one who is satisfied merely with knowledge of the scriptural meaning, being devoid of faith and the rest, or possessing only mere faith but lacking knowledge of <s>lābha</s> (attainments) and so forth — he is indeed merely a semblance of an <s>ācārya</s> and does not attain <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).

children.text: * gaṇasvarūpaṃ tarhi vācyam // GkT_1.1cd:3
children.translated_text: Then the nature of the <s>gaṇas</s> (categories) should be stated.

children.text: * ke 'ṣṭa pañcakāḥ kaś ca trikātmako gaṇaḥ ity ata āha // GkT_1.1cd:4]
children.translated_text: What are the eight groups of five, and what is the <s>gaṇa</s> whose nature is threefold? To this he says:

body.translated_text: [<s>Gaṇakārikāṭīkā</s> (Commentary on the Gaṇakārikā)]

children.text: lābhā malā upāyāś ca deśāvasthāviśuddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Lābhas</s> (attainments), <s>malas</s> (impurities), <s>upāyas</s> (means), <s>deśas</s> (places), <s>avasthas</s> (stages), <s>viśuddhis</s> (purifications),

children.text: dīkṣākāribalāny aṣṭa pañcakās trīṇi vṛttayaḥ // Gk_1.2
children.translated_text: <s>dīkṣākāris</s> (initiation-factors), <s>balas</s> (powers) — these are the eight groups of five; and three are the <s>vṛttis</s> (modes of livelihood).

body.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: * vidhīyamānam upāyaphalaṃ lābhaḥ athavā jñānatapodevanityatvasthitisiddhibhedabhinnā lābhāḥ athavānabhivyaktapūrvā bhāvāḥ sādhakātmani vyajyamānā lābhāḥ // GkT_1.2:1
children.translated_text: <s>Lābha</s> (attainment) is the fruit of the means that is enjoined; alternatively, <s>lābhas</s> are distinguished by the divisions of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>devanityatva</s> (divine constancy), <s>sthiti</s> (steadfastness), and <s>siddhi</s> (perfection); or alternatively, <s>lābhas</s> are states not previously manifest that become manifest in the self of the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner).

children.text: * yeṣām ātmāśritānāṃ bhāvānāṃ kṣapaṇārthaṃ sādhakaḥ prayatate te malāḥ // GkT_1.2:2
children.translated_text: The <s>malas</s> (impurities) are those states residing in the self for whose eradication the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) exerts effort.

children.text: * athavā mithyājñānādharmasaṅgacyutipaśutvabhedabhinnā malāḥ // GkT_1.2:3
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the <s>malas</s> are distinguished by the divisions of <s>mithyājñāna</s> (false knowledge), <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), <s>saṅga</s> (attachment), <s>cyuti</s> (fall), and <s>paśutva</s> (the state of being a bound soul).

children.text: * sādhakasya sādhakatamāḥ śuddhivṛddhihetava upāyāḥ // GkT_1.2:4
children.translated_text: The <s>upāyas</s> (means) are the most effective causes of the purification and growth of the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner).

children.text: * athavā vāsaścaryājapadhyānasadāsmṛtiprasādabhedabhinnā upāyāḥ // GkT_1.2:5
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the <s>upāyas</s> are distinguished by the divisions of <s>vāsa</s> (dwelling), <s>caryā</s> (conduct), <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>sadāsmṛti-prasāda</s> (constant remembrance and grace).

children.text: * caśabdaḥ pādapūraṇe lābhādīnāṃ vā parasparāsaṃkīrṇalakṣaṇasūtraka iti // GkT_1.2:6
children.translated_text: The word 'ca' serves as a metrical filler, or as a marker indicating that <s>lābha</s> and the rest each have mutually distinct definitions.

children.text: * deśāś cāvasthāś ca viśuddhayaś ceti dvaṃdvaḥ // GkT_1.2:7
children.translated_text: <s>Deśas</s> (places) and <s>avasthas</s> (stages) and <s>viśuddhis</s> (purifications) — this is a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound).

children.text: * yadāśrayasāmarthyena sādhakaḥ śuddhivṛddhī prāpnoti te deśā gurujanaguhāśmaśānarudralakṣaṇā iti vakṣyāmaḥ // GkT_1.2:8
children.translated_text: The <s>deśas</s> (places) are those by whose supporting power the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) attains purification and growth; we shall explain that they are characterized as the presence of the <s>guru</s> (teacher), caves, cremation grounds, and <s>Rudra</s> temples.

children.text: * ālābhaprāpter ekamaryādayāvasthitayaḥ sādhakasya avasthās tā vyaktādiviśeṣeṇa viśiṣṭā vakṣyante // GkT_1.2:9
children.translated_text: The <s>avasthas</s> (stages) of the <s>sādhaka</s> are states established within a single boundary up to the attainment of <s>lābha</s>; they will be described as distinguished by specific features beginning with <s>vyakta</s> (manifest) and so forth.

children.text: * mithyājñānādīnām atyantavyapohā viśuddhayaḥ // GkT_1.2:10
children.translated_text: The <s>viśuddhis</s> (purifications) are the complete removal of <s>mithyājñāna</s> (false knowledge) and the rest.

children.text: * dīkṣākārīṇi ca balāni ceti dvaṃdvaḥ // GkT_1.2:11
children.translated_text: <s>Dīkṣākāris</s> (initiation-factors) and <s>balas</s> (powers) — this is a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound).

children.text: * dīkṣānimittāni dīkṣākārīṇi dravyakālakriyāmūrtigurusaṃjñakāni sādhakātmagatāny upāyapravṛttinimittāni // GkT_1.2:12
children.translated_text: The <s>dīkṣākāris</s> are the factors that occasion initiation, designated as <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>kāla</s> (time), <s>kriyā</s> (action), <s>mūrti</s> (form), and <s>guru</s> (teacher); they reside in the self of the <s>sādhaka</s> and are the occasions for the commencement of the <s>upāyas</s> (means).

children.text: * balāni gurubhaktimatiprasādadvaṃdvajayadharmāpramādalakṣaṇāni // GkT_1.2:13
children.translated_text: The <s>balas</s> (powers) are characterized as devotion to the <s>guru</s>, intellect, grace, conquest of the pairs of opposites, and <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and vigilance.

children.text: * aṣṭa pañcakā ity upasaṃhāraḥ // GkT_1.2:14
children.translated_text: 'Eight groups of five' — this is the recapitulation.

children.text: * tisro vṛttaya iti prāpte trīṇi vṛttaya iti chāndasaḥ prayogaḥ kṛtaḥ pañcamalaghūkaraṇārtham // GkT_1.2:15
children.translated_text: When the expected form would be 'tisro vṛttayaḥ' (three livelihoods, feminine), the Vedic usage 'trīṇi vṛttayaḥ' is employed to make the fifth syllable light for metrical purposes.

children.text: * āgamāvirodhino 'nnārjanopāyā vṛttayaḥ bhaikṣotsṛṣṭayathālabdhasaṃjñikāḥ // GkT_1.2:16
children.translated_text: The <s>vṛttis</s> (modes of livelihood) are means of procuring food that do not contradict the <s>āgama</s> (scripture); they are designated as <s>bhaikṣa</s> (begging), <s>utsṛṣṭa</s> (discarded), and <s>yathālabdha</s> (whatever is obtained).

children.text: * tatra prathamāvasthasya tāvad bhaikṣam eva vṛttis tasyāḥ ko vidhir ity ucyate // GkT_1.2:17
children.translated_text: There, for one in the first <s>avasthā</s> (stage), the <s>vṛtti</s> is exclusively <s>bhaikṣa</s> (begging); what is the rule for that? It is stated:

children.text: * jñātvā bhikṣākālaṃ śucir bhūtvā bhasmanā hastau prakṣālya pātraṃ gṛhītvā udakaprakṣālitaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ ca kṛtvā mahādevaṃ praṇamyānujñāṃ prārthayet tadanu gurūn iti // GkT_1.2:18
children.translated_text: Having ascertained the time for begging, having become pure, having washed the hands with ash, having taken the bowl, having washed it with water and consecrated it, having bowed to <s>Mahādeva</s>, one should request permission — and then from the <s>gurus</s>.

children.text: * tato devagurubhir anujñāto mantrān āvartayan īśvarāsaktacitto vā dṛṣṭipūtena pathābhiśastapatitagṛhāṇi varjayitvā yatra ca bhayanimittaṃ ca kākādi kaluṣanimittaṃ cāmedhyavivastrayuvativiṭadurjanavacanabhikṣukākīrṇatvādy upalabhyate tadgṛhāṇy api varjayann ekam eva grāmādīnām anyatamaṃ paryaṭed yady antarāle eva paryāptir na bhavati upaghāto vā kaścid iti tataḥ svāyatanam āgatyāparādhānurūpaṃ prāyaścittaṃ kṛtvā mantrasaṃskṛtaṃ ca kṛtvā tadbhaikṣaṃ śivāyānugurave ca nivedya maheśvaraṃ hṛdi saṃdhāya saṃyatavāgudaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā samarasaṃ kṛtvoparyupari vā bhuñjīteti // GkT_1.2:19
children.translated_text: Then, having been permitted by the divine <s>gurus</s>, reciting <s>mantras</s>, or with the mind fixed on <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), traveling by a path purified by one's gaze, avoiding houses that are cursed or fallen; and also avoiding houses where fearful omens such as crows and the like, impure signs such as filth, nakedness, young women, excrement, speech of wicked people, or the presence of other mendicants are observed — one should wander through just one among the villages and so forth; if satisfaction is not obtained even along the way, or if some harm occurs, then having returned to one's own dwelling, having performed <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) appropriate to the offense, and having consecrated the food with <s>mantras</s>, one should offer that begged food to <s>Śiva</s> and to the preceptor, and then, holding <s>Maheśvara</s> in the heart, with restrained speech, facing north or facing east, having mixed the food equally or layering it, one should eat.

children.text: * pātraṃ pātraśaucaṃ ca sūtrānumataṃ smṛtiprasiddhaṃ pratipattavyam // GkT_1.2:20
children.translated_text: The bowl and the purification of the bowl should be understood as sanctioned by the <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism) and established in the <s>smṛti</s> (tradition).

children.text: * tathā ca yājñavalkyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Yājñavalkya</s> says:

children.text: * yatipātrāṇi mṛdveṇudārvalābumayāni ca /
children.translated_text: * The vessels of a <s>yati</s> (ascetic) are made of clay, bamboo, wood, or gourd; GkT_1.2:21

children.text: * salilaiḥ śuddhireteṣāṃ govālaiśca nigharṣaṇam // GkT_1.2:21
children.translated_text: * their purification is by water, and their scrubbing is with cow-hair. GkT_1.2:21

children.text: * manurapyāha /
children.translated_text: * <s>Manu</s> also says: GkT_1.2:22

children.text: * ataijasāni pātrāṇi tasya syur nirvraṇāni ca /
children.translated_text: * His vessels should be non-metallic and free from cracks; GkT_1.2:22

children.text: * teṣām adbhiḥ smṛtaṃ śaucaṃ camasānāmivādhvare // GkT_1.2:22
children.translated_text: * their purification is prescribed with water, like the <s>camasa</s> (sacrificial cups) at a sacrifice. GkT_1.2:22

children.text: * sāpannaṃ ca salepaṃ ca vibhinnaṃ cāpi yadbhavet /
children.translated_text: * That which is damaged, smeared, or even cracked — GkT_1.2:23

children.text: * tatra bhuktvā ca pītvā ca yatiścāndrāyaṇaṃ caret // GkT_1.2:23
children.translated_text: * having eaten or drunk from such, a <s>yati</s> (ascetic) should perform the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance). GkT_1.2:23

children.text: * iti yamaḥ // GkT_1.2:24
children.translated_text: * Thus says <s>Yama</s>. GkT_1.2:24

children.text: * āgamāvirodhigrahaṇād ekānnasya vidyākhyāpanānuśāsanalokayātrādibhir nimittair arjitabhaikṣasya pratiṣedho draṣṭavya ityeṣā prātipadāvasthasya vidhiḥ // GkT_1.2:25
children.translated_text: * Since the rule states "not contrary to scripture," a prohibition should be understood against food obtained for a single meal through causes such as teaching, instruction in <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), or worldly transactions — this is the rule for one in the first stage. GkT_1.2:25

children.text: * tṛtīyāvasthasyāpyayaṃ vidhiḥ // GkT_1.2:26
children.translated_text: * This rule also applies to one in the third stage. GkT_1.2:26

children.text: * etāvānatra viśeṣaḥ // GkT_1.2:27
children.translated_text: * The distinction here is only this much: GkT_1.2:27

children.text: * prāyaścittanivedanapañcabrahmajapānusnānādikaṃ na karoti tṛtīyāvasthaḥ paramayogitvāditi // GkT_1.2:28
children.translated_text: * One in the third stage does not perform <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiatory rites), <s>nivedana</s> (ritual offering), chanting of the <s>Pañcabrahma</s> (five Brahma mantras), ritual bathing, and so forth, because he is a supreme <s>yogin</s>. GkT_1.2:28

children.text: * dvitīyāvasthasyotsṛṣṭam eva vṛttiḥ // GkT_1.2:29
children.translated_text: * For one in the second stage, <s>utsṛṣṭa</s> (discarded food) alone is the means of sustenance. GkT_1.2:29

children.text: * devādyuddeśena parityaktamannapānaṃ kāruṇyakautūhalābhyāṃ vā yadi kaścid aduṣṭajātir dadyād aśucitvādidoṣarahitaṃ tadutsṛṣṭam // GkT_1.2:30
children.translated_text: * Food and drink that has been abandoned for the sake of gods and others — if someone of virtuous birth, out of compassion or curiosity, should give it, and it is free from defects such as impurity — that is called <s>utsṛṣṭa</s> (discarded). GkT_1.2:30

children.text: * tacca māyābhedenopayoktavyam // GkT_1.2:31
children.translated_text: * And that should be consumed by the method of <s>māyābheda</s> (deceptive disguise). GkT_1.2:31

children.text: * bhaikṣanivṛtteḥ pātraniyamo nāsti // GkT_1.2:32
children.translated_text: * Since begging has ceased, there is no restriction on vessels. GkT_1.2:32

children.text: * caturthāvasthasya yathālabdhaṃ vṛttiḥ // GkT_1.2:33
children.translated_text: * For one in the fourth stage, <s>yathālabdha</s> (whatever is obtained) is the means of sustenance. GkT_1.2:33

children.text: * śmaśānadeśāvasthitenaiva divase divasadvaye traye vā yad annapānaṃ prāpyate tadyathālabdham ucyate // GkT_1.2:34
children.translated_text: * Whatever food and drink is obtained while remaining in a cremation ground, over the course of one day, two days, or three — that is called <s>yathālabdha</s> (whatever is obtained). GkT_1.2:34

children.text: * pañcamāvasthasya tu śarīrābhāvādeva vṛttyanupapattiriti // GkT_1.2:35
children.translated_text: * For one in the fifth stage, however, since there is no body, the question of sustenance does not arise. GkT_1.2:35

children.text: * granthakramasya aprādhānyam arthajñānasyaiva prādhānyaṃ manyamāno'krameṇaiva nirdeśaṃ karoti gurubhaktiḥ ityādinā // GkT_1.2:36
children.translated_text: * Considering the sequence of the text to be secondary and the knowledge of meaning alone to be primary, he gives the exposition out of order, beginning with "<s>gurubhakti</s> (devotion to the teacher)" and so forth. GkT_1.2:36

children.text: * athavā sarvārambhāṇāṃ lābhārthatvāt tatprādhānyajñāpanārthaṃ pūrvam ādau lābhā uddiṣṭā idānīṃ punaḥ sarve'pi lābhā upāyasādhyāste copāyā balahīnaiḥ puruṣairanuṣṭhātuṃ na śakyanta ityataḥ prādhānyajñāpanārthaṃ balānām ādau nirdeśam āha // GkT_1.2:37]
children.translated_text: * Alternatively, since all undertakings are for the purpose of attainments, the attainments were first mentioned at the outset to indicate their primacy. Now, since all attainments are accomplished through means, and those means cannot be practiced by persons lacking strength, therefore, to indicate the primacy of the strengths, he states their exposition first. GkT_1.2:37

body.translated_text: [<s>Gaṇakārikāṭīkā</s> (Commentary on the Gaṇakārikā)]

children.text: gurubhaktiḥ prasādaś ca mater dvaṃdvajayas tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Gurubhakti</s> (devotion to the teacher), <s>prasāda</s> (clarity) of <s>mati</s> (intellect), and likewise <s>dvaṃdvajaya</s> (conquest of dualities),

children.text: dharmaś caivāpramādaś ca balaṃ pañcavidhaṃ smṛtam // Gk_1.3
children.translated_text: <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>apramāda</s> (diligence) — <s>bala</s> (strength) is remembered as fivefold. Gk_1.3

body.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: * guruḥ ācāryaḥ pañcārthajñānopadeṣṭā // GkT_1.3:1
children.translated_text: * The <s>guru</s> (teacher) is the <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor), the instructor in the knowledge of the <s>pañcārtha</s> (five categories). GkT_1.3:1

children.text: * tasya bhaktiḥ śraddhā sarvaduḥkhābhibhūtasya mamāyam eva trātety eṣā bhāvanā kāryā // GkT_1.3:2
children.translated_text: * <s>Bhakti</s> (devotion) toward him is <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) — one who is overcome by all suffering should cultivate this attitude: "This one alone is my savior." GkT_1.3:2

children.text: * tathā coktam /
children.translated_text: * And thus it has been said:

children.text: * gurur devo guruḥ svāmī ityādi na ca kāraṇapravacanayor bhaktivirodhas tadanumatyaiva tayor bhaktisambhavāt // GkT_1.3:3
children.translated_text: * "The <s>guru</s> is god, the <s>guru</s> is lord" and so forth. And there is no conflict between devotion to the <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause, i.e., God) and the <s>pravacana</s> (scripture), since devotion to both is possible only with his permission. GkT_1.3:3

children.text: * yatas tu tayor bhaktiḥ kartavyeti nānumanyate sa gurur eva na bhavati ananugrahakāritvāt // GkT_1.3:4
children.translated_text: * Indeed, a <s>guru</s> who does not approve that devotion should be rendered to both of them is not truly a <s>guru</s>, since he does not bestow grace. GkT_1.3:4

children.text: * sā ca gurubhaktis tad anabhipretam pariharatotthānādikaṃ kurvatā ca satataṃ sevanīyā // GkT_1.3:5
children.translated_text: * And that <s>gurubhakti</s> (devotion to the teacher) should be constantly practiced by avoiding what is not desired by him and performing acts of respect such as rising, and so forth. GkT_1.3:5

children.text: * jñātvā tadabhiprāyam aśāstroktam api taddhitaṃ kartavyam // GkT_1.3:6
children.translated_text: * Having understood his intention, even what is not prescribed in scripture should be done if it benefits him. GkT_1.3:6

children.text: * tathā coktam /
children.translated_text: * And thus it has been said:

children.text: * granthārthaviduṣaḥ ityādi // GkT_1.3:7
children.translated_text: * "One who knows the meaning of the texts" and so forth. GkT_1.3:7

children.text: * yad eva hi guror abhipretaṃ tad eva vihitaṃ śāstrānuktam api śreyaskari bhavati rāmasya mātṛvadhavat // GkT_1.3:8
children.translated_text: * For whatever is intended by the <s>guru</s>, that alone is enjoined; even if not stated in scripture, it becomes conducive to the highest good — like <s>Rāma</s>'s slaying of his mother. GkT_1.3:8

children.text: * guror vākyāni ca śraddheyāni anyathā doṣaśravaṇāt tattvajñānālābhaprasaṅgāc ca // GkT_1.3:9
children.translated_text: * The words of the <s>guru</s> should be trusted, for otherwise one hears of faults, and there would be the consequence of failing to obtain true knowledge. GkT_1.3:9

children.text: * bhaktibalavihīno hi grahaṇādyupeto 'pi jñānāvalepenānyathā 'pi śāstrārthaṃ pratipadyata ity ato grahaṇādyupetasya bhaktir eva balam // GkT_1.3:10
children.translated_text: * One who lacks the strength of devotion, even if endowed with learning and other qualities, through the pride of knowledge apprehends the meaning of scripture incorrectly; therefore, for one endowed with learning and other qualities, devotion alone is the true strength. GkT_1.3:10

children.text: * bhāṣyavirodho 'pi nāsti // GkT_1.3:11
children.translated_text: * Nor is there any contradiction with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary). GkT_1.3:11

children.text: * yato balam aṣṭāṅgaṃ brahmacaryam ity asyāyam arthaḥ // GkT_1.3:12
children.translated_text: * For the meaning of the statement "<s>bala</s> (strength) is the eightfold <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate discipline)" is as follows: GkT_1.3:12

children.text: * aṣṭānāṃ grahaṇādīnām aṅgam aṣṭāṅgaṃ bhaktir evocyate vedāṅgavadarthāntarābhidhānāt // GkT_1.3:13
children.translated_text: * That which is the limb (<s>aṅga</s>) of the eight — learning and the rest — is called <s>aṣṭāṅga</s> (eightfold); it is devotion itself that is meant, since it denotes something different from them, just as <s>Vedāṅga</s> (limbs of the Veda) does. GkT_1.3:13

children.text: * saiva brahmacaryanimittatvāt brahmacaryam ity ucyate // GkT_1.3:14
children.translated_text: * That very devotion is called <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate discipline) because it is the cause of <s>brahmacarya</s>. GkT_1.3:14

children.text: * yadi punar yathāśrutārthaḥ syāt tadā vāsovidhānam ityādijñāpakābhidhānavirodhaḥ syād iti // GkT_1.3:15
children.translated_text: * If, however, the literal meaning were intended, there would be a contradiction with the indicative statements such as "the rule concerning clothing" and so forth. GkT_1.3:15

children.text: * vidhāv adhikṛtasya dvitīyaṃ balam āha // GkT_1.3:16
children.translated_text: * He states the second <s>bala</s> (strength) for one engaged in the observances: GkT_1.3:16

children.text: * prasādaś ca mateḥ iti // GkT_1.3:17
children.translated_text: * "And <s>prasāda</s> (clarity) of <s>mati</s> (intellect)." GkT_1.3:17

children.text: * matiprasādaśabdenākaluṣatvam uktam // GkT_1.3:18
children.translated_text: * By the term <s>matiprasāda</s> (clarity of intellect), <s>akaluṣatva</s> (freedom from impurity) is meant. GkT_1.3:18

children.text: * sati hi tasmin matiḥ prasannā bhavati // GkT_1.3:19
children.translated_text: * For when that is present, the <s>mati</s> (intellect) becomes clear. GkT_1.3:19

children.text: * tathā ca balam akaluṣatvam iti bhāṣyam // GkT_1.3:20
children.translated_text: * And thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) states: "<s>bala</s> (strength) is <s>akaluṣatva</s> (freedom from impurity)." GkT_1.3:20

children.text: * atrāpi tarhi spaṣṭābhidhānaṃ kim arthaṃ na kṛtam // GkT_1.3:21
children.translated_text: * Then why was an explicit statement not made here as well? GkT_1.3:21

children.text: * matiprasādahetor anyasyāpy āśaucavyāmohādyabhāvasya balatvajñāpanārthaṃ pradhānāpekṣayā tv akaluṣatvam uktam // GkT_1.3:22
children.translated_text: * In order to indicate that other things too — such as the absence of ritual impurity, delusion, and so forth — which are causes of clarity of intellect, also have the nature of strength; however, <s>akaluṣatva</s> (freedom from impurity) is stated with reference to what is primary. GkT_1.3:22

children.text: * caśabdaḥ pūrvoktabalasya vidyamānasyāpi caritārthatvāt tadbalatvaṃ prādhānyān na cintyata iti sūcayati /
children.translated_text: * The word "ca" (and) indicates that even though the previously mentioned strength exists and has fulfilled its purpose, its nature as strength is not to be considered primary — GkT_1.3:23

children.text: * tac cākaluṣatvaṃ dvividhaṃ param aparaṃ ca // GkT_1.3:23
children.translated_text: * And that <s>akaluṣatva</s> (freedom from impurity) is of two kinds: supreme (<s>para</s>) and inferior (<s>apara</s>). GkT_1.3:23

children.text: * tatra kaluṣatvabījasadbhāve 'py utpannakaluṣatvanirodhi yāvad anāgataṃ kaluṣaṃ notpadyate tāvatkālaṃ yad akaluṣatvaṃ tad aparaṃ yad bījakṣayād atyantanimittasadbhāve 'pi kaluṣaṃ notpadyate tat param iti // GkT_1.3:24
children.translated_text: * Of these, that <s>akaluṣatva</s> (freedom from impurity) which suppresses arisen impurity even while the seed of <s>kaluṣatva</s> (impurity) still exists, lasting only as long as future impurity has not yet arisen — that is the inferior (<s>apara</s>). That in which, due to the destruction of the seed, impurity does not arise even when its ultimate cause is present — that is the supreme (<s>para</s>). GkT_1.3:24

children.text: * yogakriyāyām adhikṛtasya tṛtīyaṃ balam āha // GkT_1.3:25
children.translated_text: * He states the third <s>bala</s> (strength) for one engaged in <s>yogakriyā</s> (yogic practice): GkT_1.3:25

children.text: * dvaṃdvajayas tathā iti // GkT_1.3:26
children.translated_text: * "And <s>dvaṃdvajaya</s> (conquest of dualities), likewise." GkT_1.3:26

children.text: * ādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikāni duḥkhasādhanāni dvaṃdvāni teṣāṃ jayaḥ sahiṣṇutvaṃ dvaṃdvānabhibhāvyatvam ity arthaḥ // GkT_1.3:27
children.translated_text: * The causes of suffering that are <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to beings), and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to fate) are the <s>dvaṃdvas</s> (dualities); their <s>jaya</s> (conquest) means endurance — the meaning is not being overpowered by the dualities. GkT_1.3:27

children.text: * tathāśabdaḥ samānārthe // GkT_1.3:28
children.translated_text: * The word "<s>tathā</s>" (likewise) is used in the same sense. GkT_1.3:28

children.text: * yathā prāguktabale saty apy acaritārthavidhyadhikṛtasyākaluṣatvam eva balaṃ cintyate tathā baladvayasadbhāve 'py acaritārthaṃ dvaṃdvasahiṣṇutvam eva prādhānyena balaṃ cintyata iti // GkT_1.3:29
children.translated_text: * Just as when the previously mentioned strengths are present but have fulfilled their purpose, <s>akaluṣatva</s> (freedom from impurity) alone is considered the strength for one engaged in the uncompleted observances, so too when both strengths are present but have not fulfilled their purpose, endurance of dualities alone is considered the strength primarily. GkT_1.3:29

children.text: * tad api dvividhaṃ parāparabhedāt yat tāvad akṣapite pāpe yogakriyāyām abhiniviṣṭasya sādhakasya mṛdumadhyamaśītātapādibhir anubhāvyatvaṃ dhyānādyabhyāsas tad aparam // GkT_1.3:30
children.translated_text: * That too is of two kinds, by the distinction of supreme and inferior. That in which a practitioner engaged in <s>yogakriyā</s> (yogic practice), whose sin has not yet been exhausted, experiences mild and moderate cold, heat, and so forth, and practices <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and other disciplines — that is the inferior (<s>apara</s>). GkT_1.3:30

children.text: * yat kṣapite niḥśeṣapāpe guhādeśaṃ gatasyātitīvrair api śītādibhir anabhibhāvyasvalakṣaṇaṃ dvaṃdvasahiṣṇutvaṃ tat param // GkT_1.3:31
children.translated_text: * That in which one whose sin has been completely exhausted, having gone to a cave or secluded place, possesses the intrinsic characteristic of endurance of dualities, being unaffected even by extremely severe cold and the like — that is the supreme (<s>para</s>). GkT_1.3:31

children.text: * bhāṣyakṛtā tu param eva gomṛgadharmatvaṃ vyākhyātam // GkT_1.3:32
children.translated_text: * The author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary), however, has explained only the supreme form as <s>gomṛgadharmatva</s> (the conduct of cattle and deer). GkT_1.3:32

children.text: * akaluṣatvavad abhyūhya śiṣyā aparaṃ gomṛgadharmitvaṃ pratipatsyanta ity abhiprāyavatā noktam iti // GkT_1.3:33
children.translated_text: * His intention was that the disciples, inferring by analogy with <s>akaluṣatva</s> (freedom from impurity), would understand the inferior form of <s>gomṛgadharmatva</s> (conduct of cattle and deer) on their own, and therefore he did not state it. GkT_1.3:33

children.text: * sadāsmṛtyadhikṛtasya caturthaṃ balam āha dharmaś caiva iti // GkT_1.3:34
children.translated_text: * He states the fourth <s>bala</s> (strength) for one engaged in constant mindfulness: "and <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) indeed." GkT_1.3:34

children.text: * evaśabdo 'vadhāraṇe // GkT_1.3:35
children.translated_text: * The word "<s>eva</s>" (indeed) is used for emphasis. GkT_1.3:35

children.text: * yadā dharma evāvasthitas tadā balam ity arthaḥ // GkT_1.3:36
children.translated_text: * When one is established in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) alone, that is <s>bala</s> (strength) — this is the meaning. GkT_1.3:36

children.text: * īṣadadharmasadbhāve 'py avadhāraṇe nāsti doṣaḥ kṛṣṇabindusadbhāve śukla evāyaṃ paṭa iti yathā // GkT_1.3:37
children.translated_text: * Even when a slight trace of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) is present, there is no fault in the emphatic assertion, just as one says "this cloth is purely white" even when a black spot is present. GkT_1.3:37

children.text: * caśabdaḥ pūrvoktabalatrayasadbhāve 'pi dharma evācaritārthatvena balam iti sūcayati // GkT_1.3:38
children.translated_text: * The word "ca" (and) indicates that even when the three previously mentioned strengths are present, it is <s>dharma</s> alone, as the one whose purpose has not yet been fulfilled, that constitutes strength. GkT_1.3:38

children.text: * niṣṭhāyogayuktasya pañcamaṃ balam āha apramāda iti // GkT_1.3:39
children.translated_text: * He states the fifth <s>bala</s> (strength) for one engaged in the final <s>yoga</s>: "<s>apramāda</s> (diligence)." GkT_1.3:39

children.text: * viśiṣṭaṃ jñānam evātrāpramāda ity abhipretam // GkT_1.3:40
children.translated_text: * What is meant by <s>apramāda</s> (diligence) here is distinguished <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) itself. GkT_1.3:40

children.text: * tathā ca bhāṣyam asya tu jñānam asti yasmād āhāpramādī iti // GkT_1.3:41
children.translated_text: * And thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) states: "He has knowledge, therefore he is called <s>apramādī</s> (the diligent one)." GkT_1.3:41

children.text: * caśabdaḥ śarīrendriyadharmādharmavyāvṛttau satyām apramāda eva balam iti sūcayati balānāṃ nyūnādhikabhāvavyavacchedaṃ ceti // GkT_1.3:42
children.translated_text: * The word "ca" (and) indicates that when separation from body, senses, <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) has occurred, <s>apramāda</s> (diligence) alone is the strength; and it also marks the delimitation of the degrees of lesser and greater among the strengths. GkT_1.3:42

children.text: * balaṃ pañcavidham ity upasaṃhāraḥ // GkT_1.3:43
children.translated_text: * "<s>Bala</s> (strength) is fivefold" — this is the conclusion. GkT_1.3:43

children.text: * smṛtam ity āptoktatvaṃ darśayati // GkT_1.3:44
children.translated_text: * The word "<s>smṛta</s>" (remembered/declared) indicates that it is stated by authoritative teachers. GkT_1.3:44

children.text: * nanu ca tatra balacintā yujyate yatra tat sampādya śatrukṣaya upapadyate // GkT_1.3:45
children.translated_text: * Objection: Reflection on strength is appropriate only where, having cultivated it, the destruction of enemies is possible. GkT_1.3:45

children.text: * atra punar mokṣaśāstre vītarāgasya niṣparigrahasya śatrava eva na vidyante kutaḥ tatkṣaya ity ato 'tra balacintānupapanneti // GkT_1.3:46
children.translated_text: * But here, in a treatise on <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), for one who is free from passion and without possessions, there are no enemies at all — so how can there be their destruction? Therefore, reflection on strength is inappropriate here. GkT_1.3:46

children.text: * naitad evam // GkT_1.3:47
children.translated_text: * This is not so. GkT_1.3:47

children.text: * atrāpi sādhakasyājñānādiśatruhānyupapattes tatpratipādanārtham āha // GkT_1.3:48]
children.translated_text: * Here too, since the enemies of the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) — such as ignorance — arise, for the purpose of teaching about them, he says:

body.translated_text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: ajñānahānyadharmasya hāniḥ saṅgakarasya ca /
children.translated_text: The destruction of ignorance, of demerit, and of what causes attachment,

children.text: cyutihāniḥ paśutvasya śuddhiḥ pañcavidhā smṛtā // Gk_1.4
children.translated_text: the destruction of fall, and of the animal-state — purification is remembered as fivefold. // <s>Gk</s> 1.4

body.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: * ajñānahānir adharmasya iti prāpte chandobhaṅgaparihārārtham ajñānahānyadharmasyety uktam // GkT_1.4:1
children.translated_text: * When 'the destruction of ignorance, of demerit' is established [as the reading], to avoid metrical irregularity, 'ajñānahānyadharmasya' is said.

children.text: * ārṣatvān na doṣa iti // GkT_1.4:2
children.translated_text: * Because it is <s>ārṣa</s> (sage-composed), it is not a fault.

children.text: * ajñānaṃ ca vakṣyamāṇakaṃ tasya hāniḥ sabījasyātyantocchedaḥ // GkT_1.4:3
children.translated_text: * Ignorance is what will be described later; its 'destruction' means the complete eradication of that which has a seed.

children.text: * adharmo 'pi vakṣyamāṇakas tasya hāniḥ savikārasyātyantocchedaḥ // GkT_1.4:4
children.translated_text: * Demerit (<s>adharma</s>) too is what will be described later; its 'destruction' means the complete eradication of that which has its modifications.

children.text: * adharmavat saṅgakarasyāpi hānir vyākhyātā // GkT_1.4:5
children.translated_text: * Like demerit, the destruction of what causes attachment (<s>saṅgakara</s>) is also explained.

children.text: * cakāro hānipadasyānukarṣaṇārthaḥ // GkT_1.4:6
children.translated_text: * The particle 'ca' is for drawing in the word 'destruction' (<s>hāni</s>).

children.text: * cyuteḥ khalu vakṣyamāṇikāyāḥ saha bījenātyantocchedaś cyutihānir ity ucyate // GkT_1.4:7
children.translated_text: * The complete eradication of fall (<s>cyuti</s>) — which will be described later — together with its seed, is called 'the destruction of fall.'

children.text: * paśutvasyeti ṣaṣṭyantatvābhidhānād anantaroktahānipadena sambandhaḥ // GkT_1.4:8
children.translated_text: * 'Of the animal-state (<s>paśutva</s>)' — because it is stated with a genitive ending, it is connected with the word 'destruction' mentioned just before.

children.text: * ḍamarukamaṇinyāyena vā madhyoktaṃ hānipadaṃ cyutipaśutvābhyāṃ sambadhyate // GkT_1.4:9
children.translated_text: * Or, by the rule of the drum-and-jewel analogy (<s>ḍamaruka-maṇi-nyāya</s>), the word 'destruction' mentioned in the middle is connected with both 'fall' and 'animal-state.'

children.text: * cakāro vā saṅgakarapadāntokto 'trānuvṛttaḥ // GkT_1.4:10
children.translated_text: * Or, the particle 'ca' stated at the end of the word '<s>saṅgakara</s>' is resumed here.

children.text: * sa na kevalaṃ hānipadānukarṣakaḥ śuddhīnāṃ nyūnādhikabhāvaṃ vyavacchinatti // GkT_1.4:11
children.translated_text: * It not only draws in the word 'destruction' but also excludes any deficiency or excess in the [number of] purifications.

children.text: * paśutvasya māheśvaraiśvaryasambandhād ātyantiko nirodhaḥ paśutvahānir ity ucyate // GkT_1.4:12
children.translated_text: * The complete cessation of the animal-state (<s>paśutva</s>), due to its connection with the sovereignty of <s>Maheśvara</s>, is called 'the destruction of the animal-state.'

children.text: * śuddhiḥ pañcavidhā ity upasaṃhāraḥ // GkT_1.4:13
children.translated_text: * 'Purification is fivefold' — this is the conclusion.

children.text: * smṛtā ity āptoktatvapradarśanārtham // GkT_1.4:14
children.translated_text: * 'Remembered' (<s>smṛtā</s>) — this is to show that it is stated by authoritative persons.

children.text: * kiṃ punar etāḥ śatrunivṛttayo balāni cāvasthābhedabhinnasya sampadyante 'thaikāvasthasyeti // GkT_1.4:15
children.translated_text: * Now, do these removals of enemies and powers arise for one differentiated by stages, or for one who is in a single stage?

children.text: * kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ ubhayathā darśanād viṣṇucakravat // GkT_1.4:16
children.translated_text: * Whence the doubt? Because it is seen both ways, like the disc of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: * ucyate prāyeṇa tāvad avasthābhedabhinnasya yasmād avasthābhedam āha // GkT_1.4:17]
children.translated_text: * It is said: primarily for one differentiated by stages, since he teaches the stages:

body.translated_text: * [<s>Gaṇakārikāṭīkā</s> (commentary)]

children.text: vyaktāvyaktaṃ jayacchedo niṣṭhā caiveha pañcamī /
children.translated_text: Manifest, unmanifest, conquest, cutting-off, and the fifth here is completion. /

children.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>
children.translated_text: * [<s>Gaṇakārikāṭīkā</s>]

children.text: * prātipadāvasthā khalu vyaktāvasthety uktā // GkT_1.5ab:1
children.translated_text: * The first stage is called the 'manifest' (<s>vyakta</s>) stage.

body.text: * kasmāt // GkT_1.5ab:2
body.translated_text: * Why?

body.text: * pāśupatye 'yam iti vyaktinimittatvāt bhasmasnānaśayanānusnānādibhir liṅgadhārīty upadeśād iti // GkT_1.5ab:3
body.translated_text: * Because it is the cause of being manifest as a <s>Pāśupata</s> — through wearing marks such as smearing with ashes, bathing, sleeping, and re-bathing, etc., [as indicated by] the instruction 'one bearing the marks.'

body.text: * dvitīyāvasthā tu jātyādivyakter ahetutvād avyaktāvasthety uktā // GkT_1.5ab:4
body.translated_text: * But the second stage, because it is not the cause of manifestation [through signs] such as caste, is called the 'unmanifest' (<s>avyakta</s>) stage.

body.text: * kasmāt // GkT_1.5ab:5
body.translated_text: * Why?

body.text: * avyaktaliṅgopadeśād vidyādigopanopadeśāc ceti // GkT_1.5ab:6
body.translated_text: * Because of the instruction of unmanifest marks, and the instruction to conceal one's learning, etc.

body.text: * tṛtīyāvasthā punar indriyajayārthatvena jayāvasthety ucyate // GkT_1.5ab:7
body.translated_text: * The third stage, because it is for the purpose of conquering the senses, is called the 'conquest' (<s>jaya</s>) stage.

body.text: * devanityasvārthatve 'py asyā indriyajayārthataiva prādhānyenoktā sūtrāṇāṃ sambandhakathanadvāreṇācāryabhāṣyakṛteti // GkT_1.5ab:8
body.translated_text: * Though this stage also has the purpose of constant divine self-benefit, the conquest of the senses is stated as primary — through the connection of the <s>sūtras</s> as stated by the teacher, the commentary-author.

body.text: * chedāvasānārthāvasthā chedāvasthety uktā // GkT_1.5ab:9
body.translated_text: * The stage with the meaning of the cessation of cutting is called the 'cutting' (<s>cheda</s>) stage.

body.text: * sarvasya sādhakavyāpārasyātyantoparamo niṣṭhā // GkT_1.5ab:10
body.translated_text: * The absolute cessation of all the practitioner's activity is 'completion' (<s>niṣṭhā</s>).

body.text: * tadupalakṣitāvasthā niṣṭhāvasthety ucyate // GkT_1.5ab:11
body.translated_text: * The stage characterized by that is called the 'completion' stage.

body.text: * vyaktādiviśeṣaṇābhidhānādyūhādiśaktimatāṃ viśeṣapratipattir bhaviṣyatīty abhiprāyavatātrāvasthāgrahaṇaṃ na kṛtam iti // GkT_1.5ab:12
body.translated_text: * By stating the qualifiers 'manifest' etc., the intention is that those who have the power of reasoning etc. will gain particular understanding; hence the word 'stage' (<s>avasthā</s>) is not used [explicitly].

body.text: * caśabdo nyūnādhikavyavacchedasūcakaḥ // GkT_1.5ab:13
body.translated_text: * The particle 'ca' indicates the exclusion of deficiency and excess.

body.text: * pretonmattamūḍhāvasthāntarasadbhāvād adhikavyavacchedānupapattir iti cen na gopananiyamenāvyaktāvasthāyām evāntarbhāvāt // GkT_1.5ab:14
body.translated_text: * If [one objects:] since there exist other stages such as the departed, the mad, and the confused, the exclusion of excess is untenable — no, because these are included within the 'unmanifest' stage through the rule of concealment.

body.text: * jayacchedāvasthayor apy avyaktāvasthātvaprasaṅga iti cen nānayor gopananiyamānabhyupagamān niṣṭhāvasthām anabhyupagamya siddhāvasthāṃ pañcamīm āhuḥ // GkT_1.5ab:15
body.translated_text: * If [one objects:] the conquest and cutting stages too would have the nature of the 'unmanifest' stage — no, because the rule of concealment is not accepted for these. Some, without accepting the completion stage, call the fifth the 'accomplished' (<s>siddha</s>) stage.

body.text: * kecit tanmatam avadhāraṇenaiva nirācaṣṭe // GkT_1.5ab:16
body.translated_text: * Some refute their view precisely by [the word] 'indeed' (<s>eva</s>).

body.text: * niṣṭhā caiveha pañcamī iti // GkT_1.5ab:17
body.translated_text: * 'And the fifth here is completion' (<s>niṣṭhā caiveha pañcamī</s>).

body.text: * ihety asmin pañcārthadarśane niṣṭhāvasthaiva pañcamī sūtraprāmāṇyāt pratīyate na siddhāvasthā // GkT_1.5ab:18
body.translated_text: * 'Here' means in this <s>Pañcārtha</s> teaching; the fifth is indeed the completion stage, as understood from the authority of the <s>sūtras</s> — not the 'accomplished' stage.

body.text: * tatra kṣapaṇīyaprāpaṇīyābhāvāt sādhakāvasthāś ceha nirūpyante na tato 'nyasyeti // GkT_1.5ab:19
body.translated_text: * Since there is nothing to be diminished or attained [in the final stage], only the practitioner's stages are examined here, not [the stages] of others.

body.text: * atrāha // GkT_1.5ab:20
body.translated_text: * Here [an objection] is raised:

body.text: * anadhikāriṇo 'vasthāprāptir ayuktā // GkT_1.5ab:21
body.translated_text: * The attainment of a stage by one who has no qualification is unjustified.

body.text: * tatra tathā dvitīyādyavasthāprāptau jñānākaluṣatvādayo 'dhikāritvāpādakāḥ tathā prathamāvasthāprāptau ko hetur ity ucyate // GkT_1.5ab:22
body.translated_text: * For the attainment of the second and subsequent stages, [qualities such as] freedom from impurity of knowledge etc. are the qualifiers. But for the attainment of the first stage, what is the cause? It is said:

body.text: * atrāpi kāraṇaviśeṣotpāditā dīkṣā hetuḥ // GkT_1.5ab:23
body.translated_text: * Here too, initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) produced by a specific cause is the means.

body.text: * yatas tatkāraṇapratipādanārtham idam āha // GkT_1.5ab:24]
body.translated_text: * Since [he wishes to] teach that cause, he says:

body.text: dravyaṃ kālaḥ kriyā mūrtir guruś caiveha pañcamaḥ // Gk_1.5
body.translated_text: Substance, time, ritual action, image, and the <s>guru</s> as the fifth — here. // <s>Gk</s> 1.5

body.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: * atra vidyākalāpaśusaṃjñitaṃ vividhaṃ kāryaṃ dravyam ity ucyate // GkT_1.5cd:1
children.translated_text: * Here, what is called 'substance' (<s>dravya</s>) is the manifold effect designated as <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>kalā</s> (ritual materials), and <s>paśu</s> (the initiand).

children.text: * tatra vidyā tāvac chiṣyagatā dīkṣāṅgaṃ yayā śiṣyo dīkṣādhikṛto bhavati // GkT_1.5cd:2
children.translated_text: * Of these, <s>vidyā</s> first — it is the component of initiation residing in the disciple, by which the disciple becomes qualified for initiation.

children.text: * yayā tv ācāryaḥ sampūrṇāṃ dīkṣāṃ nirvartayati sācāryagatā vidyā // GkT_1.5cd:3
children.translated_text: * The <s>vidyā</s> by which the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) completes the full initiation resides in the teacher.

children.text: * kalā darbhādyā dīkṣāṅgam // GkT_1.5cd:4
children.translated_text: * <s>Kalā</s> means <s>darbha</s> grass and such — a component of initiation.

children.text: * uktaṃ hi darbhāḥ punar bhasma candanaṃ sūtram eva ca // GkT_1.5cd:5
children.translated_text: * For it has been said: '<s>Darbha</s> grass, ashes, sandalwood, and thread indeed,

children.text: * puṣpāṇi ca punar dhūpam eṣa kramaḥ smṛtaḥ // GkT_1.5cd:6
children.translated_text: * and flowers, and incense — this is the remembered order.'

children.text: * paśuḥ saṃskartavyo brāhmaṇaḥ // GkT_1.5cd:7
children.translated_text: * <s>Paśu</s> is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who is to be consecrated [i.e., the initiand].

children.text: * itthaṃ vyākhyānakaraṇād upakaraṇāder api saṃgraha ity ato na saṃskārakārikāvirodhaḥ // GkT_1.5cd:8
children.translated_text: * By explaining in this way, the instruments etc. are also included; hence there is no contradiction with the consecration verse.

children.text: * kālaḥ pūrvāhṇaḥ // GkT_1.5cd:9
children.translated_text: * Time means the forenoon.

children.text: * kāraṇamūrtiśiṣyayoḥ saṃskārakarma kriyety ucyate // GkT_1.5cd:10
children.translated_text: * The consecration ritual involving the cause, the image, and the disciple is called 'action' (<s>kriyā</s>).

children.text: * tatkramaś ca saṃskārakārikāyāṃ draṣṭavyaḥ // GkT_1.5cd:11
children.translated_text: * Its order is to be seen in the consecration verse.

children.text: * mūrtiśabdena yad upahārasūtre mahādevejyāsthānam ūrdhvaliṅgādilakṣaṇaṃ vyākhyātaṃ tatsamīpadakṣiṇabhūpradeśaḥ kuṭyādyavyavahito 'trābhipretaḥ // GkT_1.5cd:12
children.translated_text: * By the word 'image' (<s>mūrti</s>) is meant the place of worship of <s>Mahādeva</s> as explained in the <s>Upahāra-sūtra</s> — characterized by the upward-facing <s>liṅga</s> etc.; specifically, the ground to the south near it, unobstructed by walls etc.

children.text: * gurur ācāryaḥ sa dvividhaḥ parāparabhedāt // GkT_1.5cd:13
children.translated_text: * The <s>guru</s> is the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>); he is of two kinds, through the distinction of higher and lower.

children.text: * tatrāparaḥ pañcārthajñānamaryādānvitaḥ // GkT_1.5cd:14
children.translated_text: * The lower [<s>guru</s>] is endowed with the knowledge of the five categories (<s>pañcārtha</s>) and [their] boundaries.

children.text: * tathā coktam /
children.translated_text: * And thus it is said:

children.text: * śāstrānuge pracāre yo 'bhiniviṣṭaḥ prakṛṣṭadhīḥ kuśalaḥ /
children.translated_text: * 'He who is devoted to practice in accordance with the scriptures, of superior intellect, and skilled —

children.text: * sa bhavati mataḥ kila satām ācāryo jñānahetuś ca // GkT_1.5cd:15
children.translated_text: * he is considered by the virtuous to be the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) and the cause of knowledge.'

children.text: * tathā /
children.translated_text: * And also:

children.text: * ācāre sthāpayan śiṣyān yasmād ācarati svayam /
children.translated_text: * 'Since he establishes disciples in proper conduct and himself practices,

children.text: * ācinoti ca śāstrārthān ācāryas tena kīrtyate // GkT_1.5cd:16
children.translated_text: * and gathers the meanings of the scriptures — he is called the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>).'

children.text: * tasyādhiṣṭhātā bhagavān maheśvaraḥ paro gurus tathā caivaṃ varṇite nimittam apy atra nānuktaṃ bhavati // GkT_1.5cd:17
children.translated_text: * His overseer is the Blessed Lord <s>Maheśvara</s>, the supreme <s>guru</s>; and when thus described, the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>) too is not left unstated.

children.text: * caśabdo nyūnādhikavyavacchedasūcakaḥ // GkT_1.5cd:18
children.translated_text: * The particle 'ca' indicates the exclusion of deficiency and excess.

children.text: * evaśabdo guroḥ prādhānyam avadhārayati // GkT_1.5cd:19
children.translated_text: * The particle '<s>eva</s>' determines the primacy of the <s>guru</s>.

children.text: * iha iti svasiddhāntanirdeśaḥ // GkT_1.5cd:20
children.translated_text: * 'Here' (<s>iha</s>) indicates [this] own doctrinal system.

children.text: * pañcama ity upasaṃhāraḥ // GkT_1.5cd:21
children.translated_text: * 'The fifth' — this is the conclusion.

children.text: * athavā eva iha padayoḥ pāṭhaviparyayaṃ kṛtvānyathārthaḥ pradarśyate // GkT_1.5cd:22
children.translated_text: * Or, by transposing the words '<s>eva</s>' and '<s>iha</s>,' a different meaning is shown:

children.text: * ihaiva pāśupatadarśane evaṃviśiṣṭāni dīkṣānimittāni nānyatra // GkT_1.5cd:23
children.translated_text: * In this very <s>Pāśupata</s> teaching alone are these specific causes of initiation [found], not elsewhere.

children.text: * tataś ca niṣpādyā dīkṣāpy atraiva viśiṣṭāsti nānyatrety uktaṃ bhavati // GkT_1.5cd:24
children.translated_text: * And from this, the initiation accomplished is also distinguished only here, not elsewhere — this is what is stated.

children.text: * atha kiṃ kāraṇaviśeṣair eveyaṃ dīkṣā viśiṣyate na kiṃ tarhi phalaviśeṣair api // GkT_1.5cd:25
children.translated_text: * Now, is this initiation distinguished only by the specific causes, or also by specific results?

children.text: * yasmāt tadartham idam āha // GkT_1.5cd:26]
children.translated_text: * Since [the answer is also by results], for that purpose he says:

body.translated_text: * [<s>Gaṇakārikāṭīkā</s>]

children.text: jñānaṃ tapo 'tha nityatvaṃ sthitiḥ siddhiś ca pañcamī /
children.translated_text: Knowledge, austerity, then permanence, stability, and the fifth is accomplishment. / <s>Gk</s> 1.6ab

children.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>
children.translated_text: * [<s>Gaṇakārikāṭīkā</s>]

children.text: * tatra pañcapadārthaviṣayaṃ samāsavistaravibhāgaviśeṣopasaṃhāranigamanatas tattvajñānaṃ prathamo vidyālābho jñānam iti cocyate // GkT_1.6ab:1
children.translated_text: * Of these, the knowledge of the five categories — through summary, detailed explanation, analysis, specification, conclusion, and ascertainment — the knowledge of reality, which is the first attainment of <s>vidyā</s>, is called 'knowledge' (<s>jñāna</s>).

body.text: * teṣāṃ samāsādīnāṃ svarūpaṃ yady api śrīmatācāryeṇa bhāṣyāvasāne prakaṭitaṃ tathāpi leśatas tadbhāṣyavivaraṇārtham asmābhir apy ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:2
body.translated_text: * Although the form of these — summary etc. — has been made clear by the revered teacher at the end of the commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>), nevertheless, for the purpose of elucidating that commentary, we too state it briefly.

body.text: * tatra padārthānām uddeśaḥ samāsaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:3
body.translated_text: * Of these, the enumeration of the categories is the 'summary' (<s>samāsa</s>).

body.text: * so 'tha śabdādibhir duḥkhāntādīnām abhihitaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:4
body.translated_text: * This [summary] is stated by the words '<s>atha</s>' ('now') etc., [through terms like] 'the end of suffering' etc.

body.text: * uddiṣṭānāṃ pramāṇataḥ prapañcābhidhānaṃ vistaraḥ // GkT_1.6ab:5
body.translated_text: * The detailed description with proofs of what has been enumerated is the 'detailed explanation' (<s>vistara</s>).

body.text: * patiḥ saṃnādya ity evamādi // GkT_1.6ab:6
body.translated_text: "The Lord, having united [them]" and so forth.

body.text: * tatsādhanatvena pramāṇāny api vistaraśabdenoktāni // GkT_1.6ab:7
body.translated_text: The <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) are also stated by the word "vistara" (elaboration) as being the means for that [end of suffering].

body.text: * dharmadharmiṇāṃ yathāsambhavaṃ lakṣaṇato 'nyatvābhidhānaṃ vibhāgaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:8
body.translated_text: The statement of otherness, that is, distinction in terms of definition of <s>dharmas</s> (properties) and <s>dharmins</s> (property-bearers) as appropriate, is <s>vibhāga</s> (division).

body.text: * sarvatrāpy abhidhīyata ity abhidhānam // GkT_1.6ab:9
body.translated_text: That which is stated everywhere is <s>abhidhāna</s> (designation).

body.text: * karmavyutpattir draṣṭavyā // GkT_1.6ab:10
body.translated_text: The etymological derivation should be understood as a <s>karmavyutpatti</s> (action-based derivation).

body.text: * tatra duḥkhāntasya vibhāgas tāvad ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:11
body.translated_text: Among these, the division of <s>duḥkhānta</s> (end of suffering) is stated first.

body.text: * sarvaduḥkhāpoho duḥkhāntaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:12
body.translated_text: <s>Duḥkhānta</s> is the removal of all suffering.

body.text: * sa dvividho 'nātmakaḥ sātmakaś ceti // GkT_1.6ab:13
body.translated_text: That is twofold: <s>anātmaka</s> (without self) and <s>sātmaka</s> (with self).

body.text: * tatrānātmakaḥ sarvaduḥkhānām atyantocchedaḥ sātmakas tu maheśvaraiśvaryalakṣaṇā siddhiḥ // GkT_1.6ab:14
body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>anātmaka</s> type is the absolute cessation of all sufferings, while the <s>sātmaka</s> type is the <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) characterized by the sovereignty of <s>Maheśvara</s>.

body.text: * sā dvirūpā jñānaśaktiḥ kriyāśaktiś ceti // GkT_1.6ab:15
body.translated_text: That [<s>siddhi</s>] is of two forms: <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge) and <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action).

body.text: * tatra jñānam eva śaktir jñānaśaktiḥ // GkT_1.6ab:16
body.translated_text: Among these, knowledge itself as power is <s>jñānaśakti</s>.

body.text: * sā khalv ekāpi satī samastavyastaviṣayabhedāt pañcadhoktā darśanaśravaṇetyādinā brahmāder ivopacaritasarvajñatvapratiṣedhārtham // GkT_1.6ab:17
body.translated_text: Although it is one, it is described as fivefold—through seeing, hearing, and so forth—due to the distinction between collective and individual objects, in order to negate the attributed omniscience of <s>Brahmā</s> and others.

body.text: * kriyāhetuḥ śaktiḥ kriyāśaktiḥ sā trividhā manojavitvādibhedā // GkT_1.6ab:18
body.translated_text: The power that is the cause of action is <s>kriyāśakti</s>; that is threefold, with divisions such as <s>manojavitva</s> (swiftness of mind) and others.

body.text: * tatra niratiśayaṃ śīghrakāritvaṃ manojavitvaṃ karmādinirapekṣasyecchayaivānantararūpakartṛtvādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ kāmarūpitvaṃ saṃbhṛtakāyendriyasyāpi niratiśayaiśvaryasambandhitvaṃ vikaraṇadharmitvaṃ ceti // GkT_1.6ab:19
body.translated_text: Among these, unsurpassed swiftness of action is <s>manojavitva</s>; the capacity to be the agent and controller of the immediately succeeding form by mere will alone, without dependence on <s>karma</s> and the like, is <s>kāmarūpitva</s> (ability to assume any form at will); the quality of having an unsurpassed connection with sovereignty even when one's body and senses are fully assembled is <s>vikaraṇadharmatva</s> (the quality of being beyond instruments).

body.text: * yadā ceyaṃ dvirūpā siddhiḥ prāpyate tadā daśa siddhilakṣaṇāny avaśyatvādīni patitvāntāni bhavanti // GkT_1.6ab:20
body.translated_text: When this twofold <s>siddhi</s> is attained, then there arise ten characteristics of <s>siddhi</s>, beginning with <s>avaśyatva</s> and ending with <s>patitva</s>.

body.text: * tatra niratiśayamaparādhīnatvam avaśyatvam // GkT_1.6ab:21
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>avaśyatva</s> is unsurpassed non-dependence on others.

body.text: * atha kim idam avaśyatvaṃ nāmeti // GkT_1.6ab:22
body.translated_text: Now, what is this so-called <s>avaśyatva</s>?

body.text: * vaśyatvamalanivṛttāvaśyatvākhyaḥ puruṣe 'vasthito dharmo 'bhivyajyate paṭe śuklatāvad ity eke // GkT_1.6ab:23
body.translated_text: Some say: the quality called <s>avaśyatva</s>, established in the <s>puruṣa</s> (self), is manifested upon the removal of the impurity of subjugation (<s>vaśyatvamala</s>), just as whiteness is manifested in a cloth.

body.text: * tac cāyuktam aiśvaryābhivyakteḥ pratiṣiddhatvād anātmakasya ca dharmasyābhivyaktyanupapatter anyathānātmakatvavirodhaḥ syād yadā guṇair yukta ityādi bhāṣyavirodhāc ca nāvasthitābhivyaktiḥ kiṃ tv aiśvaryasambandha eva parādhīnatvanivartakatvād avaśyatvam ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:24
body.translated_text: That is not correct, because the manifestation of sovereignty is denied [in this system], and because the manifestation of a quality that is <s>anātmaka</s> (non-self) is impossible—otherwise there would be a contradiction with the <s>anātmaka</s> nature; and also because it contradicts the <s>bhāṣya</s> passage "when endowed with qualities" and so forth. Therefore, <s>avaśyatva</s> is not a pre-established quality that is manifested, but rather the very connection with sovereignty that removes dependence on others is called <s>avaśyatva</s>.

body.text: * athavā yadā guṇair yuktas tadā sa evātathābhūtapūrvas tathā bhavati sarpaśikyādivat tasya bhāvas tatsvarūpam avaśyatvaṃ bhedanocyate vyavahārārtham ity evam anāveśyatvādiṣv api vicāro draṣṭavyaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:25
body.translated_text: Or alternatively, when [the self] is endowed with qualities, that very one who was not previously in such a state becomes so, like a rope-snake [analogy]; the nature of that state is <s>avaśyatva</s>. The distinction is stated for practical purposes. The same analysis should be applied to <s>anāveśyatva</s> and the other [characteristics] as well.

body.text: * satkāryavicāre cāyaṃ vistārito mayā teneha na pratanyate // GkT_1.6ab:26
body.translated_text: This has been elaborated by me in the investigation of <s>satkārya</s> (pre-existent effect); therefore it is not expanded upon here.

body.text: * sattvāntarānabhibhāvyajñānasambandhitvam anāveśyatvaṃ sattvāntarādhīnajīvitarahitatvam avadhyatvam samastabhayātikrāntatvam abhayatvam aiśvaryeṇa nityasambandhitvam akṣayatvaṃ kāyendriyavaikalyaphalenātyantāsambandhitvam ajaratvaṃ prāṇādiviyogajaduḥkhāsaṃsparśitvam amaratvaṃ sarvatrābhipretārtheṣu pravartamānasya maheśvareṇāpy apratibandhadharmitvam apratīghātaḥ sarvapaśubhyo 'bhyadhikatvam aiśvaryātiśayān mahattvaṃ sarvapaśvādikāryasvāmitvaṃ patitvam iti // GkT_1.6ab:27
body.translated_text: The quality of having knowledge that cannot be overpowered by other beings is <s>anāveśyatva</s>; freedom from dependence on other beings for one's life is <s>avadhyatva</s>; having transcended all fear is <s>abhayatva</s>; having an eternal connection with sovereignty is <s>akṣayatva</s>; absolute non-association with the fruits of deficiency of body and senses is <s>ajaratva</s>; being untouched by the suffering arising from separation of <s>prāṇa</s> and the like is <s>amaratva</s>; having the quality of being unobstructed even by <s>Maheśvara</s> when engaging in all desired aims is <s>apratīghāta</s>; being superior to all <s>paśus</s> (bound souls) through the excellence of sovereignty is <s>mahattva</s>; being the master of all <s>paśus</s> and their effects is <s>patitva</s>.

body.text: * yad asvatantraṃ tat sarvakāryaṃ tasya vibhāga ucyate vidyā kalā paśuś ceti // GkT_1.6ab:28
body.translated_text: That which is dependent is all effect; its division is stated as <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>kalā</s> (material category), and <s>paśu</s> (bound soul).

body.text: * tatra paśuguṇo vidyā svaśāstradṛṣṭyoktā // GkT_1.6ab:29
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>vidyā</s> is the quality of the <s>paśu</s>, as stated from the perspective of this [Pāśupata] system.

body.text: * vaiśeṣikadṛṣṭyā dravyavat // GkT_1.6ab:30
body.translated_text: From the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> perspective, [it is] like a substance.

body.text: * sā dvidhā bodhābodhasvabhāvabhedāt // GkT_1.6ab:31
body.translated_text: That is twofold, due to the distinction between the nature of awareness (<s>bodha</s>) and non-awareness (<s>abodha</s>).

body.text: * tatrābodhasvabhāvā dharmādilakṣaṇā vidyāntarbhāvakaraṇād avidyātmakasya vidyāntarbhāve kalāder apy antarbhāvaḥ syād iti // GkT_1.6ab:32
body.translated_text: Among these, the non-awareness type, characterized by <s>dharma</s> and the like—if by including it under <s>vidyā</s>, what is of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> is included under <s>vidyā</s>, then <s>kalā</s> and the like would also have to be included.

body.text: * bodhasvabhāvā tu viṣayabhedāc caturdhā pañcadhā coktā // GkT_1.6ab:33
body.translated_text: The awareness type, however, is stated as fourfold or fivefold due to the distinction of objects.

body.text: * svarūpatas tu dvidhā vivekavṛttiḥ sāmānyavṛttiś ceti // GkT_1.6ab:34
body.translated_text: But in its own nature, it is twofold: <s>vivekavṛtti</s> (discriminative cognition) and <s>sāmānyavṛtti</s> (general cognition).

body.text: * tatra vivekavṛttiḥ prāyeṇopadeśavyaṅgyā na ca tatra samākhyāntaram asti // GkT_1.6ab:35
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>vivekavṛtti</s> is mostly revealed through instruction, and there is no other designation for it.

body.text: * vidyaiva hi viśeṣasamākhyā sāmānyavṛttis tu pramāṇamātravyaṅgyā cittam ity uktā // GkT_1.6ab:36
body.translated_text: For <s>vidyā</s> itself is the specific designation; <s>sāmānyavṛtti</s>, however, which is revealed through the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) alone, is called <s>citta</s> (mind).

body.text: * anayor bhedaṣ ṭīkāntare mayā darśita neha pradarśyate // GkT_1.6ab:37
body.translated_text: The distinction between these two has been shown by me in another commentary; it is not demonstrated here.

body.text: * cetanānāśritatve sati niścetanā kalā // GkT_1.6ab:38
body.translated_text: <s>Kalā</s> is non-sentient, being defined as that which does not depend on consciousness.

body.text: * sāpi dvividhā kāryākhyā karaṇākhyā ceti // GkT_1.6ab:39
body.translated_text: That also is twofold: called <s>kārya</s> (effect/product) and called <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument).

body.text: * tatra kāryākhyā daśavidhā pṛthivyaptejovāvyākāśagandharasarūpasparśaśabdalakṣaṇā karaṇākhyā tu trayodaśavidhā pañca karmendriyāṇi pañca buddhīndriyāṇy antaḥkaraṇatrayaṃ ceti // GkT_1.6ab:40
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>kāryākhyā</s> (the effect type) is tenfold: earth, water, fire, air, <s>ākāśa</s> (space), smell, taste, form, touch, and sound; the <s>karaṇākhyā</s> (the instrument type) is thirteenfold: five <s>karmendriyas</s> (organs of action), five <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (organs of cognition), and the three <s>antaḥkaraṇas</s> (internal organs).

body.text: * paśutvasambandhī paśuḥ // GkT_1.6ab:41
body.translated_text: <s>Paśu</s> (bound soul) is that which is connected with <s>paśutva</s> (the state of bondage).

body.text: * so 'pi dvividhaḥ sāñjano nirañjanaś ceti // GkT_1.6ab:42
body.translated_text: That too is twofold: <s>sāñjana</s> (with impurity) and <s>nirañjana</s> (without impurity).

body.text: * tatra sāñjanaḥ śarīrendriyasambandhī caturdaśavidhaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:43
body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>sāñjana</s> type, connected with body and senses, is fourteenfold.

children.text: * uktaṃ hi daivam aṣṭavidhaṃ jñeyaṃ tairyagyonaṃ ca pañcadhā /
children.translated_text: As it has been said: "The divine types are to be known as eightfold, and the animal types as fivefold;

children.text: * parvam ekaṃ tu mānuṣyam etat saṃsāramaṇḍalam // GkT_1.6ab:44
children.translated_text: There is one human type—this is the circle of <s>saṃsāra</s>."

body.text: * iti nirañjanas tu trividhaḥ saṃhṛtaḥ kaivalyagato niṣṭhāyogayuktaś ceti // GkT_1.6ab:45
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>nirañjana</s> type is threefold: the withdrawn (<s>saṃhṛta</s>), the one who has attained <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation), and the one established in <s>niṣṭhāyoga</s> (final yoga).

body.text: * samastasṛṣṭisaṃhārānugrahakāri kāraṇaṃ tasyaikasyāpi guṇadharmabhedād vibhāga ukto 'nyatpatitvam ityādinā // GkT_1.6ab:46
body.translated_text: The cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>) that performs the creation, dissolution, and grace of all [beings]—even though it is one, its division is stated due to the distinction of qualities and attributes, by [expressions] such as "<s>patitva</s>" (lordship) and so forth.

body.text: * niratiśayadṛkkriyāśaktiḥ patitvaṃ tenaiśvaryeṇa nityasambandhitvaṃ sattvam anāgantukaiśvaryatvam ādyatvaṃ samastajanmarahitatvam ajātatvaṃ mahāsṛṣṭisaṃhārakartṛtvaṃ bhavodbhavatvaṃ paramotkṛṣṭaṃ guṇadharmanimittanāmābhidheyatvaṃ vāmatvaṃ duḥkhāntanimittadharmotpādakanāmābhidheyatvaṃ vā svecchayaivāśeṣakāryotpattyādikāraṇasvabhāvaḥ krīḍā taddharmitvaṃ devatvaṃ siddhasādhakapaśubhyaḥ paratvaṃ jyeṣṭhatvaṃ sargādāv api rutabhayasaṃyojakatvaṃ rudratvam karmādinirapekṣasya svecchayaivāśeṣakāryakartṛtvaṃ kāmitvaṃ śamasukhanirvāṇakaratvaṃ śaṃkaratvam antarasṛṣṭyām api saṃhārakartṛtvaṃ kālatvaṃ kāryakāraṇākhyānāṃ kalānāṃ sthānaśarīrādibhāvena saṃyojakatvaṃ kalavikaraṇatvaṃ dharmādibalānāṃ yatheṣṭaṃ vṛttilābhalopākṣepakartṛtvaṃ balapramathanatvaṃ sarvadevamānuṣatiraścāṃ ratirañjanādhivāsanākartṛtvaṃ sarvabhūtadamanatvaṃ sakalaniṣkalāvasthāyās tulyaśaktitvaṃ manomanastvaṃ sukhakarānantaśarīrādhiṣṭātṛtvam aghoratvaṃ duḥkhakarānantaśarīrādhiṣṭātṛtvaṃ ghorataratvaṃ sarvavidyādikāryāṇāṃ vyāptādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ pūraṇaṃ yathepsitānantaśarīrādikaraṇaśaktiḥ pauruṣyam // GkT_1.6ab:47
body.translated_text: Unsurpassed power of seeing and action is <s>patitva</s>; eternal connection with that sovereignty is <s>sattva</s>; having sovereignty that is not adventitious is <s>ādyatva</s>; being free from all births is <s>ajātatva</s>; being the agent of the great creation and dissolution is <s>bhavodbhavatva</s>; being designated by the name whose cause is the supremely exalted quality-attribute is <s>vāmatva</s>; or, being designated by the name whose cause is the attribute that produces the end of suffering is [also <s>vāmatva</s>]; the nature of being the cause by one's own will alone of the origination etc. of all effects is <s>krīḍā</s> (play), and having that quality is <s>devatva</s>; being superior to <s>siddhas</s>, <s>sādhakas</s>, and <s>paśus</s> is <s>jyeṣṭhatva</s>; having the quality of joining [beings] with sound, fear at the beginning of creation is <s>rudratva</s>; being the agent of all effects by one's own will alone without dependence on <s>karma</s> etc. is <s>kāmitva</s>; producing the happiness of tranquility and <s>nirvāṇa</s> is <s>śaṃkaratva</s>; being the agent of dissolution even during intermediate creation is <s>kālatva</s>; joining the <s>kalās</s> called effect and cause with [bound souls] in the form of location, body, etc. is <s>kalavikaraṇatva</s>; being the agent of granting, removing, and directing the operation of the powers of <s>dharma</s> and the like as desired is <s>balapramathanatva</s>; being the agent of delighting, coloring, and habituating all gods, humans, and animals is <s>sarvabhūtadamanatva</s>; having equal power in both the <s>sakala</s> (with parts) and <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts) states is <s>manomanastva</s>; being the controller of infinite blissful bodies is <s>aghoratva</s>; being the controller of infinite suffering-producing bodies is <s>ghorataratva</s>; being the pervading controller of all <s>vidyā</s> and other effects is <s>pūraṇa</s>; the power to create bodies and instruments as desired without limit is <s>pauruṣya</s>.

body.text: * tad ubhayaṃ bhagavataḥ puruṣatvam ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:48
body.translated_text: Both of those together are called the <s>puruṣatva</s> (personhood) of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord).

body.text: * sarvapaśvādibhyo 'bhyadhikotkṛṣṭavyatiriktatvaṃ mahattvaṃ devatvaṃ pūrvoktam // GkT_1.6ab:49
body.translated_text: Being superior, exalted, and distinct from all <s>paśus</s> and the like is <s>mahattva</s>; <s>devatva</s> has been explained earlier.

body.text: * duḥkhāntanimittaṃ dhyānaikaviṣayatvam oṃkāratvam // GkT_1.6ab:50
body.translated_text: Being the sole object of meditation for the purpose of ending suffering is <s>oṃkāratva</s>.

body.text: * ṛṣitvaṃ kriyāśaktir jñānaśaktis tu vipratvam // GkT_1.6ab:51
body.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣitva</s> is the <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action), while <s>vipratva</s> is the <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge).

body.text: * anayor āśrayavyāpitvānantaviṣayatvaniratiśayatvajñāpanārthaṃ tadāśrayo bhagavān mahān ity uktaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:52
body.translated_text: In order to indicate that these two have unlimited scope, infinite objects, and unsurpassed nature, their substratum, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, is called "<s>Mahān</s>" (the Great One).

body.text: * sarvadā sarvatrāvicalitasvabhāvena vartamāno bhagavān eṣa ity ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:53
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, who exists at all times and in all places with an unchanging nature, is called "<s>Eṣa</s>" (this one).

body.text: * guṇadharmadvāreṇa vācaḥ pravartante yasmād atas tadvyatiriktas tadaviśeṣitaś ca bhagavān viśuddha ity ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:54
body.translated_text: Since words operate through the medium of quality-attributes, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who is distinct from and uncharacterized by those [qualities], is called "<s>Viśuddha</s>" (the Pure One).

children.text: * nityānāgantukaiśvaryayukte paramakāraṇe /
children.translated_text: With regard to the supreme cause that is eternally connected with non-adventitious sovereignty,

children.text: * yatra vāco nivartante vāgviśuddhaḥ sa kīrtitaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:55
children.translated_text: Where words turn back—He is proclaimed as "<s>Vāgviśuddha</s>" (pure beyond speech).

children.text: * kṣaṇaikam api yas tatra prāpnoty ekāgratāṃ yatiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>yati</s> (ascetic) who attains one-pointed concentration there even for a single moment,

children.text: * sa dagdhvā sarvakarmāṇi śivasāyujyam āpnuyāt // GkT_1.6ab:56
children.translated_text: Having burned all <s>karmas</s>, attains union with <s>Śiva</s> (<s>Śivasāyujya</s>).

body.text: * sarvaiśvaryapradātṛtvaṃ maheśvaratvaṃ samastakāryaviṣayaṃ prabhutvam īśatvaṃ sarvavidyāviṣayaṃ prabhutvam īśānatvaṃ sarvabhūtaviṣayaṃ prabhutvam īśvaratvam // GkT_1.6ab:57
body.translated_text: The quality of bestowing all sovereignty is <s>Maheśvaratva</s> (supreme lordship); mastery over all effects is <s>Pabhutva</s> (lordship); <s>Īśatva</s> (rulership) is mastery over all sciences; <s>Īśānatva</s> is mastery over all beings; <s>Īśvaratva</s> is [mastery over all]. // GkT_1.6ab:57

body.text: * prakramāpekṣaḥ khalv evam īśādiśabdānām arthaḥ pradarśito 'nyathā punar ekārthatvam eveti // GkT_1.6ab:58
body.translated_text: The meaning of the words <s>Īśa</s> and others has been shown thus according to the context; otherwise, they are indeed synonymous. // GkT_1.6ab:58

body.text: * brahmagrahaṇasyodāharaṇārthatvād aśeṣapativiṣayaprabhutvam adhipatitvaṃ bṛṃhaṇabṛhattvaṃ brahmatvaṃ paripūrṇaparitṛptatvaṃ śivatvam iti // GkT_1.6ab:59
body.translated_text: Since the mention of <s>Brahman</s> is for the purpose of illustration: mastery over all domains of lordship is <s>Adhipatitva</s> (overlordship); expansion and greatness is <s>Brahmatva</s> (the nature of <s>Brahman</s>); the state of being complete and satisfied is <s>Śivatva</s> (the nature of <s>Śiva</s>). // GkT_1.6ab:59

body.text: * evaṃ suniścitāḥ khalv ime guṇadharmāḥ parameśvarasyopahārakāle gāyatā bhāvayitavyāḥ satataṃ vā japaṃ ca kurvatā vibhaktyupasarganipātakriyāpadānām arthaiḥ saha cintanīyās tato 'cireṇaiva kālena śuddhivṛddhī bhavataḥ // GkT_1.6ab:60
body.translated_text: Thus, these divine qualities (<s>guṇadharma</s>) of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) are firmly established. By one who sings at the time of offering, they should be meditated upon; or by one who constantly performs <s>japa</s> (recitation), they should be contemplated along with the meanings of case-endings, prefixes, particles, and verbal forms. Then, before long, purification and progress occur. // GkT_1.6ab:60

body.text: * te ca svātmasaṃvedye iti // GkT_1.6ab:61
body.translated_text: And those [purification and progress] are self-evident. // GkT_1.6ab:61

body.text: * dharmārthaḥ sādhakavyāpāro vidhiḥ // GkT_1.6ab:62
body.translated_text: The purpose of the <s>dharma</s> (religious practice), the practitioner's activity, is <s>vidhi</s> (prescribed procedure). // GkT_1.6ab:62

body.text: * sa dvividhaḥ pradhānabhūto guṇabhūtaś ceti // GkT_1.6ab:63
body.translated_text: That is of two kinds: principal and subsidiary. // GkT_1.6ab:63

body.text: * tatrāvyavadhānena dharmahetur yo vidhiḥ sa pradhānabhūtaś caryeti vakṣyate // GkT_1.6ab:64
body.translated_text: Among those, the procedure that is the direct cause of <s>dharma</s> (spiritual merit) is the principal one, called <s>caryā</s> (religious observance), as will be explained. // GkT_1.6ab:64

body.text: * yas tu caryānugrāhakaḥ sa guṇabhūto 'nusnānādiḥ // GkT_1.6ab:65
body.translated_text: But that which supports the <s>caryā</s> is the subsidiary [procedure], such as bathing and so forth. // GkT_1.6ab:65
