body.text: * tatra bhuktocchiṣṭādinimittāyogyatāpratyayanivṛttyarthaṃ liṅgābhivyaktyarthaṃ ca yat snānaṃ yat kaluṣanivṛttyarthaṃ tad upasparśanam // GkT_1.6ab:66
body.translated_text: Among those, the bathing that is for the purpose of removing the notion of unfitness caused by eating leftovers and the like, and for the purpose of displaying the [Śaiva] mark — that which is for the purpose of removing impurity — is <s>upasparśana</s> (ritual ablution). // GkT_1.6ab:66

body.text: * etad ubhayam apy ajapataiveśvaraniyogam anusaṃdhāya saṃsāradoṣaṃ bhāvayatā gurulaghubhāvaṃ ca paryālocya bhasmanaiva kartavyam // GkT_1.6ab:67
body.translated_text: Both of these [bathing and ablution] should be performed with sacred ash alone, while silently recalling the command of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), contemplating the defects of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), and considering the nature of heaviness and lightness [of actions]. // GkT_1.6ab:67

body.text: * nirmālyadhāraṇam api liṅgābhivyaktibhaktivṛddhidvāreṇa caryānugrāhakam // GkT_1.6ab:68
body.translated_text: The wearing of <s>nirmālya</s> (sacred offerings) also supports the <s>caryā</s> through the avenue of displaying the [Śaiva] mark and increasing devotion. // GkT_1.6ab:68

body.text: * vicārya kāraṇanirmālyaṃ niṣparigrahaṃ paraṃ kṛtaṃ gṛhītvā saṃyatātmanā kāraṇaṃ praṇamyānujñāṃ prārthayet tataḥ prasannamukhaṃ bhagavantaṃ svanirmālyaṃ nirmalīkaraṇāya prayacchantaṃ dhyātvā mahāprasāda ity abhisaṃdhāya bhaktyaiva śirasi dhārayet // GkT_1.6ab:69
body.translated_text: Having reflected, one should take the <s>nirmālya</s> of the Cause [i.e., <s>Śiva</s>], which is without attachment and supreme, with a disciplined self. Having bowed to the Cause and requested permission, then, meditating on the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord) with a pleased countenance offering his own <s>nirmālya</s> for purification, one should bear it on the head with devotion alone, thinking 'This is great grace.' // GkT_1.6ab:69

body.text: * tathāyatanavāsitvam api caryānugrāhakam // GkT_1.6ab:70
body.translated_text: Likewise, dwelling in a sacred precinct (<s>āyatana</s>) also supports the <s>caryā</s>. // GkT_1.6ab:70

children.text: * tathā coktam /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said:

children.text: * dharmakṣetraṃ paraṃ hy etac chivāyatanaṃ bhuvi /
children.translated_text: 'For this is the supreme <s>Dharmakṣetra</s> (field of merit), the abode of <s>Śiva</s> on earth;

children.text: * vidhibījasya sā bhūmis tatra vaptam mahāphalam // GkT_1.6ab:71
children.translated_text: It is the soil for the seed of ritual procedure; what is sown there yields great fruit.' // GkT_1.6ab:71

children.text: * liṅgāddhastaśataṃ sāgraṃ śivakṣetraṃ samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A hundred [measures] and more from the <s>liṅga</s> (sacred emblem) is the sacred domain of <s>Śiva</s> on all sides;

children.text: * jantūnāṃ tatra pañcatvaṃ śivasāyujyakāraṇam // GkT_1.6ab:72
children.translated_text: The death of beings there is the cause of union with <s>Śiva</s>.' // GkT_1.6ab:72

body.text: * grāme vā yadi vetyādi // GkT_1.6ab:73
body.translated_text: 'Whether in a village or elsewhere' and so on. // GkT_1.6ab:73

body.text: * upasparśanenākṣapitakaluṣakṣāpaṇārthaṃ prāṇāyāmaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:74
body.translated_text: <s>Prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) is for the purpose of destroying the impurity not destroyed by <s>upasparśana</s> (ablution). // GkT_1.6ab:74

body.text: * koṣṭhasya vāyor gatinirodhaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:75
body.translated_text: <s>Prāṇāyāma</s> is the restraint of the movement of the breath in the trunk. // GkT_1.6ab:75

body.text: * tatropaspṛśya kāraṇatīrthakaragurūn anupraṇamya prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vā padmakasvastikādīnām anyatamaṃ yathāsukham āsanaṃ baddhvā kṛtam unnataṃ ca kṛtvā śanaiḥ saṃyatāntaḥkaraṇena recakādīn kuryāt // GkT_1.6ab:76
body.translated_text: In that practice, having performed ablution, having bowed to the Cause, the sacred ford, and the teachers, facing east or north, having adopted any comfortable seat such as the lotus or <s>svastika</s> posture, having made [the body] firm and erect, one should gently perform <s>recaka</s> (exhalation) and the other [phases] with a controlled inner faculty. // GkT_1.6ab:76

body.text: * kaluṣābhāve 'pi cittasyātinirmalatvāpādanārtham abhyāsārthaṃ nityaṃ kuryāt // GkT_1.6ab:77
body.translated_text: Even when there is no impurity, for the purpose of producing extreme purity of mind and for the sake of practice, one should perform [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>] constantly. // GkT_1.6ab:77

children.text: * uktaṃ hi /
children.translated_text: For it has been said:

children.text: * prāṇāyāmair dahed doṣān dhāraṇābhiś ca kilbiṣam /
children.translated_text: 'By <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> one should burn away defects; by <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), sins;

children.text: * pratyāhāreṇa viṣayān dhyānenānīśvarān guṇān // GkT_1.6ab:78
children.translated_text: By <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of senses), sense-objects; by <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), non-divine qualities.' // GkT_1.6ab:78

children.text: * prāṇāyāmena yuktasya viprasya niyatātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the disciplined <s>vipra</s> (twice-born) who is devoted to <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, with a controlled self,

children.text: * sarve doṣāḥ praṇaśyanti sattvasthaś caiva jāyate // GkT_1.6ab:79
children.translated_text: All defects perish, and he becomes established in [pure] being.' // GkT_1.6ab:79

children.text: * jalabindukuśāgreṇa māse māse ca yaḥ pibet /
children.translated_text: 'He who month by month drinks a drop of water on the tip of a <s>kuśa</s> grass

children.text: * saṃvatsaraśataṃ sāgraṃ prāṇāyāmaikatatsamam // GkT_1.6ab:80
children.translated_text: For a hundred years and more — that equals a single <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.' // GkT_1.6ab:80

children.text: * prāṇāyāmaviśuddhātmā yasmāt paśyati tatparam /
children.translated_text: 'Since one whose self is purified by <s>prāṇāyāma</s> sees that Supreme [Reality],

children.text: * tasmāt kiṃcit paraṃ nāsti prāṇāyāmād iti śrutiḥ // GkT_1.6ab:81
children.translated_text: There is nothing higher than <s>prāṇāyāma</s> — thus says the <s>Śruti</s> (revelation).' // GkT_1.6ab:81

body.text: * tadakṣapitakaluṣakṣapaṇārthaṃ japaḥ kartavyaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:82
body.translated_text: For the purpose of destroying the impurity not destroyed by that [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>], <s>japa</s> (recitation) should be performed. // GkT_1.6ab:82

body.text: * tṛtīyacaturthayor anyatarasmin brahmaṇi prayatnaniruddhaṃ cittaṃ sampūrṇākṣarānubodhena tadarthānubodhena vā punaḥ punaḥ saṃcārayed iti // GkT_1.6ab:83
body.translated_text: In either the third or fourth [meaning of] <s>Brahman</s>, one should repeatedly direct the mind — which has been restrained through effort — toward the full understanding of the syllables or toward the understanding of their meaning. // GkT_1.6ab:83

body.text: * evaṃ ca prāyaścittāntaram utsūtratvān na kartavyam iti // GkT_1.6ab:84
body.translated_text: And thus, any other <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) should not be performed, as it would be extra-scriptural. // GkT_1.6ab:84

body.text: * nanu ca trikasya kaluṣanivṛttyartham evābhidhānaṃ vyabhicārāntareṣu punaḥ kiṃ prāyaścittam // GkT_1.6ab:85
body.translated_text: Now, if the triad [of ablution, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, and <s>japa</s>] is taught precisely for the purpose of removing impurity, then what expiation [is there] for other transgressions? // GkT_1.6ab:85

body.text: * na caitad vācyaṃ yater apramattasya sarvadaiva saṃyatatvād asambhavī vyabhicāra iti kāmādivyabhicāreṇa samānatvāt trikasyāpy anārambhaprasaṅgo vā // GkT_1.6ab:86
body.translated_text: One should not say this — [namely] that since an ascetic who is vigilant is always self-controlled, transgression is impossible for him — because it is analogous to transgression through desire and the like, and there would be the absurd consequence of not undertaking the triad either. // GkT_1.6ab:86

body.text: * kiṃ cādharmasāmarthyād viduṣo 'pi vyabhicārasambhavāt // GkT_1.6ab:87
body.translated_text: Moreover, because transgression is possible even for the wise, due to the power of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness). // GkT_1.6ab:87

body.text: * uktaṃ ca hriyate budhyamāno 'pi ityādi // GkT_1.6ab:88
body.translated_text: And it has been said: 'Even one who understands is carried away' and so on. // GkT_1.6ab:88

body.text: * hiṃsāyāś cāvaśyaṃbhāvitvāt // GkT_1.6ab:89
body.translated_text: And because harm [to living beings] is inevitable. // GkT_1.6ab:89

children.text: * uktaṃ hi /
children.translated_text: For it has been said:

children.text: * ahṇā rātryā ca yāñ jantūn nihanty ajñānato yatiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever creatures an ascetic unknowingly kills by day and by night,

children.text: * teṣāṃ snātvā viśuddhyarthaṃ prāṇāyāmān ṣaḍ ācaret // GkT_1.6ab:90
children.translated_text: For their purification, having bathed, he should perform six <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.' // GkT_1.6ab:90

body.text: * pratidinam ity arthaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:91
body.translated_text: The meaning is: daily. // GkT_1.6ab:91

body.text: * atraike sarvavyabhicāreṣu trikam eva kartavyam iti manyante // GkT_1.6ab:92
body.translated_text: Here, some think that the triad alone should be performed for all transgressions. // GkT_1.6ab:92

body.text: * vayaṃ tu paśyāmaḥ kaluṣanivṛttyartham eva trikaṃ kartavyam // GkT_1.6ab:93
body.translated_text: But we see [it thus]: the triad should be performed for the purpose of removing impurity alone. // GkT_1.6ab:93

body.text: * bhāṣyasyāpi tathaiva śrutatvān nādṛṣṭārtham adṛṣṭaśuddheś cāniścayāt trikānuparamaprasaṅgaḥ syāt tasmāt kaluṣanivṛttau pūrvakṛtādharmakṣapaṇavad vyabhicārakṛtādharmakṣapaṇārtham api vidhyācaraṇam eva kartavyam // GkT_1.6ab:94
body.translated_text: Since even the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) has been heard in that way, and since there is no certainty about unseen purification, there would be the absurd consequence of never ceasing the triad. Therefore, just as the triad removes the <s>adharma</s> accumulated previously, so too for the purpose of destroying the <s>adharma</s> caused by transgression, the performance of prescribed ritual and <s>yoga</s> alone should be undertaken — not any other expiation. // GkT_1.6ab:94

body.text: * tathā ca sūtraṃ bhūyas tapaś caret iti // GkT_1.6ab:95
body.translated_text: And thus the <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism) says: 'One should perform further <s>tapas</s> (austerity).' // GkT_1.6ab:95

children.text: * manur apy āha /
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s> also says:

children.text: * yat kiṃcid enaḥ kurvanti vāṅmanomūrtibhir janāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever sin people commit through speech, mind, or body,

children.text: * tat sarvaṃ nirṇudanty āśu tapasaiva tapodhanāḥ // GkT_1.6ab:96
children.translated_text: All that the rich in austerity quickly dispel through <s>tapas</s> alone.' // GkT_1.6ab:96

children.text: * mahāpātakinaś caiva śeṣāś cākāryakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even great sinners and others who perform forbidden acts

children.text: * tapasaiva sutaptena mucyante kilbiṣāt tataḥ // GkT_1.6ab:97
children.translated_text: Are freed from their sins through well-performed <s>tapas</s>.' // GkT_1.6ab:97

children.text: * tathā śrīmadbhāṣyakṛtāpi jñāpakam uktam /
children.translated_text: And the illustrious author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) has also stated an indicator:

children.text: * tapobhir āryā nirṇudanti pāpaṃ dhyānopayogāt kṣapayanti puṇyam /
children.translated_text: 'The noble ones dispel sin through austerities; through the practice of meditation they destroy merit;

children.text: * te nirmalās tattvavido viśuddhā gacchanti mokṣaṃ hy ubhayor abhāvāt // GkT_1.6ab:98
children.translated_text: They, stainless, knowers of reality, purified, attain <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) through the absence of both.' // GkT_1.6ab:98

body.text: * na cāyaṃ niyamaḥ puṇyakṣaya eva dhyānāt kiṃtu pāpakṣayo 'pi // GkT_1.6ab:99
body.translated_text: And this rule does not [mean] that meditation destroys only merit, but also sin. // GkT_1.6ab:99

body.text: * yataḥ tatraiva jñāpakāntaram uktam // GkT_1.6ab:100
body.translated_text: Because therein another indicator has been stated: // GkT_1.6ab:100

children.text: * sarvaṃ dahati dhyānena puṇyapāpakriyāśrayam /
children.translated_text: 'Meditation burns everything that is the basis of merit-and-sin-producing action;

children.text: * puṇyapāpaphale dagdhe svāmī tasya na vidyate // GkT_1.6ab:101
children.translated_text: When the fruits of merit and sin are burned, no master of them remains.' // GkT_1.6ab:101

body.text: * iti // GkT_1.6ab:102
body.translated_text: Thus. // GkT_1.6ab:102

body.text: * evaṃ tarhy anarthakaṃ vidhyanuṣṭhānam iti cen nānena vidhinā rudrasamīpaṃ gatveti pravacanād vidhyanuṣṭhānavikalasya yogānuṣṭhānasāmarthyābhāvāt // GkT_1.6ab:103
body.translated_text: If [one objects] that in that case the performance of prescribed ritual (<s>vidhi</s>) is pointless — no, because the scripture says 'having gone near <s>Rudra</s> through this ritual,' and because one who lacks the performance of ritual does not have the capacity for the practice of <s>yoga</s>. // GkT_1.6ab:103

children.text: * tathā cānyatrāpy uktam /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said elsewhere:

children.text: * dharmaḥ prayatnataḥ kāryo yoginā tu viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dharma</s> should be practiced with effort, especially by the <s>yogin</s>;

children.text: * nāsti dharmād ṛte yoga iti yogavido viduḥ iti // GkT_1.6ab:104
children.translated_text: There is no <s>yoga</s> without <s>dharma</s> — thus know the knowers of <s>yoga</s>.' // GkT_1.6ab:104

body.text: * tasmād upasparśanādibhiḥ prasannaṃ cittaṃ kṛtvā sarvasyādharmasya kṣapaṇārthaṃ vidhiyogānuṣṭhānam evātyantādyabhiyogena kartavyaṃ na prāyaścittāntaram iti // GkT_1.6ab:105
body.translated_text: Therefore, having purified the mind through ablution and the like, for the destruction of all <s>adharma</s>, the performance of prescribed ritual and <s>yoga</s> alone should be undertaken with supreme and constant effort — not any other expiation. // GkT_1.6ab:105

body.text: * tathā daśāhiṃsādayo yamāś caryānugrāhakā yadā tadā vidhyantarbhūtā yadā tu yogakriyānugrāhakās tadā yogāntarbhūtā iti // GkT_1.6ab:106
body.translated_text: And thus the ten [observances] beginning with <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence), the <s>yamas</s> (restraints), support the <s>caryā</s> when they are part of the prescribed ritual; but when they support <s>yogakriyā</s> (yogic practice), they are part of <s>yoga</s>. // GkT_1.6ab:106

body.text: * tatra vākkāyamanobhiḥ paraduḥkhānutpādanam ahiṃsā indriyasaṃyamo brahmacaryaṃ dharmasādhanānaṅgavacanapratiṣedhaḥ satyaṃ varṇāśramibhiḥ saha dṛṣṭārthasaṃgatipratiṣedho 'saṃvyavahāraḥ dharmasādhanāṅgād abhyadhikasya nyāyato 'py asvīkaraṇam anyāyatas tu dharmasādhanāṅgasyāpy asvīkaraṇaṃ cāsteyaṃ parair apakṛtasyāpy amlānacittatvam akrodhaḥ vākkāyamanobhir gurau hitabhāvenaiva vartanaṃ guruśuśrūṣā kāyāntaḥkaraṇātmaśuddhiḥ śaucaṃ svavṛttyaivopārjitānnasya vidhiyogānuṣṭhānāvirodhenābhyavaharaṇam āhāralāghavam // GkT_1.6ab:107
body.translated_text: Among these, non-production of suffering for others through speech, body, and mind is <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence); restraint of the senses is <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy); the prohibition of speech that is not part of the means of <s>dharma</s> is <s>satya</s> (truthfulness); the prohibition of association with those of the <s>varṇāśrama</s> system for visible purposes is <s>asaṃvyavahāra</s> (non-intercourse); the non-acceptance even by rightful means of anything in excess of what is part of the means of <s>dharma</s>, and the non-acceptance by unrightful means of even that which is part of the means of <s>dharma</s>, is <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing); having an untroubled mind even when wronged by others is <s>akrodha</s> (non-anger); serving the teacher through speech, body, and mind with solely beneficial intent is <s>guruśuśrūṣā</s> (service to the teacher); purification of the body, inner faculty, and self is <s>śauca</s> (cleanliness); eating food earned by one's own livelihood in a manner that does not conflict with the performance of prescribed ritual and <s>yoga</s> is <s>āhāralāghava</s> (moderation in diet).

body.text: * aṣṭau grāsā muner iti kecit tan neṣṭaṃ vidhiyogānuṣṭhānavirodhaprasaṅgāt // GkT_1.6ab:108
body.translated_text: Some say "eight morsels for a sage," but that is not accepted, because it would entail a conflict with the performance of prescribed ritual and <s>yoga</s>.

body.text: * savyañjanāśanodakābhyāṃ koṣṭhasya bhāgatrayaṃ pūrayitvā caturthaṃ bhāgaṃ vāyoḥ saṃcaraṇārtham avaśeṣayed ity anye // GkT_1.6ab:109
body.translated_text: Others say: having filled three-quarters of the stomach with food containing condiments and water, one should leave the fourth quarter for the circulation of air.

body.text: * tad iṣṭam evāvirodhāt // GkT_1.6ab:110
body.translated_text: That is accepted, as there is no conflict.

body.text: * atra ca pañcavidhabhaikṣābhidhāyakaṃ vākyaṃ caren mādhukarīm ityādy avirodhena vyākhyeyam // GkT_1.6ab:111
body.translated_text: And here, the statement prescribing the fivefold begging, beginning with "one should practice the bee-like [begging]" (<s>mādhukārī</s>), should be explained in a manner that avoids conflict.

body.text: * yathāvihitavidhiyogānuṣṭhāne satatam evodyamo 'pramādaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:112
body.translated_text: Constant diligence in the performance of prescribed ritual and <s>yoga</s> as enjoined is <s>apramāda</s> (vigilance).

body.text: * ayaṃ ca pradhānabhūto yamaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:113
body.translated_text: And this is the principal <s>yama</s> (restraint).

children.text: * tathā coktam /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said:

children.text: * yatidharmasya sadbhāvaḥ śrūyatāṃ guṇadoṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Hear about the existence of the <s>yati</s> (ascetic)'s <s>dharma</s> in terms of merits and defects:

children.text: * apramādāt parā siddhiḥ pramādān narakaṃ dhruvam // GkT_1.6ab:114
children.translated_text: From vigilance comes the highest <s>siddhi</s> (attainment); from negligence, certainly hell."

children.text: * iti /
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * vāso 'pi jñānotpādanadvāreṇa caryānugrāhakatvād guṇavidhir eveti // GkT_1.6ab:115
children.translated_text: Even <s>vāsa</s> (dwelling) is indeed a <s>guṇavidhi</s> (secondary injunction), because it supports the <s>caryā</s> (practice) through the medium of producing knowledge.

body.text: * cittadvāreṇeśvarasambandhaḥ puruṣasya yogaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:116
body.translated_text: The connection of the <s>puruṣa</s> (self) with <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) through the medium of <s>citta</s> (mind) is <s>yoga</s>.

body.text: * sa dvividhaḥ kriyālakṣaṇaḥ kriyoparamalakṣaṇaś ceti // GkT_1.6ab:117
body.translated_text: That is twofold: characterized by action (<s>kriyālakṣaṇa</s>) and characterized by the cessation of action (<s>kriyoparamalakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: * tatra kriyālakṣaṇo japayantraṇadhāraṇadhyānasmaraṇātmaka iti // GkT_1.6ab:118
body.translated_text: Among these, the type characterized by action consists of <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>yantraṇa</s> (restraint), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>smaraṇa</s> (remembrance).

body.text: * vakṣyāmaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:119
body.translated_text: We shall explain [this further].

body.text: * kriyoparamalakṣaṇo 'py atigatyādiśabdavācya iti // GkT_1.6ab:120
body.translated_text: The type characterized by the cessation of action is also denoted by the words <s>atigati</s> (transcendence) and the like.

body.text: * śāstrāntaroktapadārthebhyo 'mīṣām atiśayābhidhānaṃ viśeṣaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:121
body.translated_text: The distinction of these [categories] from the categories taught in other systems is their superior characterization (<s>viśeṣa</s>).

body.text: * tathāhi śāstrāntare duḥkhanivṛttir eva duḥkhāntaḥ iha tu paramaiśvaryaprāptiś ca // GkT_1.6ab:122
body.translated_text: For example, in other systems <s>duḥkhānta</s> (end of suffering) is merely the cessation of suffering, whereas here it also includes the attainment of supreme sovereignty.

body.text: * tathānyatrābhūtvā bhāvi kāryam iha tu nityaṃ paśvādi // GkT_1.6ab:123
body.translated_text: Similarly, elsewhere the effect is that which comes into being after not having existed, whereas here <s>paśu</s> (the bound soul) and the like are eternal.

body.text: * tathānyatrāsvatantraṃ pradhānādi kāraṇam iha tu svatantro bhagavān eva // GkT_1.6ab:124
body.translated_text: Similarly, elsewhere the cause is a dependent [entity] like <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), whereas here the cause is the independent <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord) alone.

body.text: * tathānyatra kaivalyābhyudayaphalo yogaḥ iha tu paramaduḥkhāntaphalaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:125
body.translated_text: Similarly, elsewhere <s>yoga</s> has liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) and worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) as its fruits, whereas here it has the supreme <s>duḥkhānta</s> as its fruit.

body.text: * tathānyatrāvartakaḥ svargādiphalo vidhir iha tv anāvartako rudrasamīpādiphala iti // GkT_1.6ab:126
body.translated_text: Similarly, elsewhere the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) has fruits such as heaven from which there is return, whereas here it has fruits such as proximity to <s>Rudra</s> from which there is no return.

body.text: * padārthānāṃ samāptisaṃhāras tatra duḥkhakāryakāraṇavidhīnām iti śabdena samāptir uktā // GkT_1.6ab:127
body.translated_text: The conclusion (<s>saṃhāra</s>) of the categories is the completion of suffering, effect, cause, and injunction—their completion is stated by the word "iti."

body.text: * yogasya tu tvāśabdeneti // GkT_1.6ab:128
body.translated_text: And the completion of <s>yoga</s> is [stated] by the word "tvā."

body.text: * samāptānāṃ niḥśeṣīkaraṇārthaṃ prāsaṅgikasaṃśayanivṛttyarthaṃ ca dharmāntarābhidhānaṃ nigamanam // GkT_1.6ab:129
body.translated_text: The <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion) is the statement of additional matters for the purpose of completely exhausting the topics already concluded and for the purpose of removing incidental doubts.

body.text: * pratijñātārthena sahaikavākyatvakhyāpanārtham ity anye // GkT_1.6ab:130
body.translated_text: Others say: it is for the purpose of indicating the syntactic unity with the stated topic.

body.text: * tad evaṃ vidhiyogayoḥ kāryāntarbhāve 'pi atiprayojanavaśāt pṛthagabhidhānaṃ kṛtvā pañcānām eva samāsādaya uktā ity ataḥ pañcaiva padārthā ucyante // GkT_1.6ab:131
body.translated_text: Thus, although <s>vidhi</s> (injunction) and <s>yoga</s> are included within <s>kārya</s> (effect), they are stated separately due to their special purposes; having been stated in a compound of [all] five, only five categories are taught.

body.text: * anye tu padārthabhedam anyathā varṇayanti // GkT_1.6ab:132
body.translated_text: Others, however, describe the division of categories differently.

body.text: * tattvaṃ guṇo bhāva iti // GkT_1.6ab:133
body.translated_text: [They enumerate them as:] <s>tattva</s> (reality), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>bhāva</s> (state).

body.text: * tatra yad anāśritaṃ tat tattvam // GkT_1.6ab:134
body.translated_text: Among these, that which is independent is <s>tattva</s>.

body.text: * tac ca viṃśatibhedam // GkT_1.6ab:135
body.translated_text: And that has twenty divisions.

body.text: * pañca pṛthivyādīni trayodaśendriyāṇi paśuḥ kāraṇaṃ ceti // GkT_1.6ab:136
body.translated_text: [Namely:] the five [elements] beginning with earth, the thirteen <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), and <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause).

body.text: * tattvavṛttayaḥ bhāvāśrayā guṇās tatra pṛthivyādiṣu yathāsambhavaṃ rūparasagandhasparśaśabdāḥ pañcaiva vartante // GkT_1.6ab:137
body.translated_text: The modes of the <s>tattvas</s> (realities), which depend on <s>bhāva</s> (existence), are <s>guṇas</s> (qualities); among these, in earth and the other [elements], there exist, as appropriate, only five: form, taste, smell, touch, and sound.

body.text: * indriyatattvāni tu nirguṇāni // GkT_1.6ab:138
body.translated_text: The <s>indriya-tattvas</s> (sense-organ realities), however, are without qualities.

body.text: * paśuṣu sapta guṇā vartante paśutvadharmādharmacittavidyāprayatnecchālakṣaṇāḥ // GkT_1.6ab:139
body.translated_text: In the <s>paśus</s> (bound souls), seven qualities exist, characterized by <s>paśutva</s> (bondage), <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>adharma</s> (demerit), <s>citta</s> (mind), <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>prayatna</s> (effort), and <s>icchā</s> (desire).

body.text: * sukhādīnāṃ tu tadvikāratvāt tadantarbhāva eva mṛdvikāravat // GkT_1.6ab:140
body.translated_text: But pleasure and the like, being modifications of those [qualities], are included within them, just as [products] of clay [are included within clay].

body.text: * kāraṇe trayo guṇāḥ kāmārthitvavipratvākhyā iti dharmibhyo 'nyānanyatvenānirvacanīyāḥ // GkT_1.6ab:141
body.translated_text: In the <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause/Lord), there are three qualities, called <s>kāmārthitva</s> and <s>vipratva</s>—they are indefinable as either identical with or different from their substrates.

body.text: * sattvaguṇānāṃ dharmā bhāvā ity ucyante // GkT_1.6ab:142
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> (properties) of existing things and qualities are called <s>bhāvas</s> (states/modes of being).

body.text: * tadvicāraś ca satkāryavicāre kṛte iti neha kriyate // GkT_1.6ab:143
body.translated_text: And the investigation of that has been done in the investigation of <s>satkārya</s> (pre-existent effect); therefore it is not done here.

body.text: * tad evaṃ kāraṇādiniścayajñānaṃ prathamo lābha iti // GkT_1.6ab:144
body.translated_text: Thus, the ascertaining knowledge of the cause and the like is the first <s>lābha</s> (attainment).

body.text: * dvitīyaṃ lābham āha tapaḥ iti // GkT_1.6ab:145
body.translated_text: He states the second <s>lābha</s>: "<s>tapas</s> (austerity)."

body.text: * bhasmasnānādividhijanito dharmas tapa ity ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:146
body.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> produced by the prescribed practices such as bathing in ashes is called <s>tapas</s>.

body.text: * tasyotpādo rakṣaṇādiliṅgād api niścīyate // GkT_1.6ab:147
body.translated_text: Its production is also ascertained from signs such as protection.

body.text: * adharmataskareṇa sanmārgād apahriyamāṇaḥ sādhakaḥ purapālasthānīyena dharmeṇa rakṣyate // GkT_1.6ab:148
body.translated_text: The practitioner being carried away from the right path by the thief of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) is protected by <s>dharma</s>, which stands in the position of a city-guardian.

body.text: * avasthānād avasthāntaragamanaṃ gatiḥ // GkT_1.6ab:149
body.translated_text: Movement from one state to another state is <s>gati</s> (progression).

body.text: * vihitānuṣṭhāna eva saṃtoṣaḥ prītiḥ // GkT_1.6ab:150
body.translated_text: Contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>) in the performance of what has been enjoined is <s>prīti</s> (joy).

body.text: * lābhasambandhaḥ prāptiḥ // GkT_1.6ab:151
body.translated_text: Connection with attainment is <s>prāpti</s> (acquisition).

body.text: * yadbalena vidhiyogābhiniviṣṭasya cittaṃ rambhādīnāṃ gītavādyādibhir api kṣobhayituṃ na śakyate tanmāhātmyaṃ dharmaśaktir ity arthaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:152
body.translated_text: The power of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmaśakti</s>) is that by the force of which the mind of one who is engaged in prescribed ritual and <s>yoga</s> cannot be disturbed even by the singing, music, and other [allurements] of <s>Rambhā</s> and the like — that is the meaning of <s>māhātmya</s> (greatness).

body.text: * atigatisāyujyasthitiśabdā niṣṭhāyogaparyāyāḥ // GkT_1.6ab:153
body.translated_text: The words <s>atigati</s> (transcendence), <s>sāyujya</s> (union), and <s>sthiti</s> (stability) are synonyms of <s>niṣṭhāyoga</s> (final yoga).

body.text: * yasmin sati padārthāḥ sādhakasyādhyakṣopalabdhiyogyā bhavanti sa prakāśaḥ dvividhaḥ parāparabhedāt // GkT_1.6ab:154
body.translated_text: That by which the categories become fit for the practitioner's direct perception is <s>prakāśa</s> (illumination); it is twofold, due to the distinction of higher and lower.

body.text: * tatra yena vidhiyogasādhanāni samyag vivecayati dhyeyatattve brahmaṇi ca svaṃ cittaṃ samāhitaṃ cyutaṃ ca cyavamānaṃ ca lakṣayati so 'paraḥ prakāśaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:155
body.translated_text: Among these, the lower <s>prakāśa</s> is that by which one properly discriminates the means of prescribed ritual and <s>yoga</s>, and perceives one's own mind as concentrated on the object of meditation—<s>Brahman</s>—as well as when it has fallen away or is falling away.

body.text: * yena tu sthāpanāvasare sarvatattvāni saguṇadharmāṇy ānantyena dṛṣṭvā yojyāyojyabhāvena vivecayati sa para iti // GkT_1.6ab:156
body.translated_text: The higher [<s>prakāśa</s>] is that by which, at the time of establishment, one sees all realities together with their qualities and attributes in their infinity and discriminates them in terms of what is to be connected and what is not to be connected.

body.text: * viṣayiṇām iṣṭaviṣayeṣv ivānicchato 'pi rudre cittavṛttipravāhaḥ samīpaṃ tad evātyantotkarṣāpannaṃ devanityatvam ity etat sarvaṃ dharmajñāpakatvenoktam iti // GkT_1.6ab:157
body.translated_text: Just as for sense-enjoyers there is a flow of mental activity toward desired objects, so too there is an involuntary flow of mental activity toward <s>Rudra</s>—this proximity, having attained the utmost excellence, is <s>devanityatva</s> (eternal devotion to God). All of this has been stated as indicating <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: * tṛtīyaṃ lābham āha // GkT_1.6ab:158
body.translated_text: He states the third <s>lābha</s> (attainment).

body.text: * atha nityatvam iti // GkT_1.6ab:159
body.translated_text: "Now, <s>nityatva</s> (constancy)."

body.text: * athetyānantarye tapo'nantaraṃ yad deve bhāvābhyāsalakṣaṇaṃ nityatvaṃ tṛtīyo lābhaḥ sa ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:160
body.translated_text: The word "now" [indicates] succession: the <s>nityatva</s> toward the Lord, characterized by habitual contemplation (<s>bhāvābhyāsa</s>), which follows upon <s>tapas</s>, is the third <s>lābha</s>—that is stated.

body.text: * na tu nityayuktatety arthaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:161
body.translated_text: But the meaning is not "eternally connected."

body.text: * avyucchinnapravāho nityatvam atrābhipretaṃ yathā nityapravāhā gaṅgetī // GkT_1.6ab:162
body.translated_text: What is intended here by <s>nityatva</s> is an uninterrupted flow, just as [one says] "the <s>Gaṅgā</s> has an eternal flow."

body.text: * caturthaṃ lābham āha sthitir iti // GkT_1.6ab:163
body.translated_text: He states the fourth <s>lābha</s>: "<s>sthiti</s> (stability)."

body.text: * doṣahetujālebhyaś chinnasya mūlākhyānivṛttau cittasya rudre 'vasthānam atyantaniścalatvaṃ sthitir ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:164
body.translated_text: <s>Sthiti</s> is said to be the absolutely immovable resting of the mind in <s>Rudra</s>, when the root [cause] called <s>mūlā</s> (ignorance) of the web of causes of defects has been cut off.

body.text: * tatsamakālaṃ yogino 'saṅgitvādīni nava lakṣaṇāni bhavanti // GkT_1.6ab:165
body.translated_text: Simultaneously with that, nine characteristics arise in the <s>yogin</s>, beginning with <s>asaṅgitva</s> (non-attachment).

body.text: * tatra lakṣyamāṇasya saṅgasyātyantavyāvṛttir asaṅgitvam // GkT_1.6ab:166
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>asaṅgitva</s> is the absolute cessation of the attachment that is being perceived.

body.text: * kevalarudratattvāvasthiticittattvaṃ yogitvam // GkT_1.6ab:167
body.translated_text: <s>Yogitva</s> (the state of being a yogin) is the state of mind established solely in the reality of <s>Rudra</s>.

body.text: * anurudhyamānacittavṛttitvaṃ nityātmatvam // GkT_1.6ab:168
body.translated_text: <s>Nityātmatva</s> (eternal selfhood) is having a mental activity that is in accord [with <s>Rudra</s>].

body.text: * aprādurbhāvicittatvam ajatvam // GkT_1.6ab:169
body.translated_text: <s>Ajatva</s> (unborn-ness) is having a mind that does not manifest [outwardly].

body.text: * paramasamatā maitratvam // GkT_1.6ab:170
body.translated_text: <s>Maitratva</s> (friendliness) is supreme equanimity.

body.text: * śarīrādiviyuktatvam ekatvam // GkT_1.6ab:171
body.translated_text: <s>Ekatva</s> (oneness) is being separated from the body and the like.

body.text: * sarvāśaṅkāsthānātikrāntatvaṃ kṣemitvam // GkT_1.6ab:172
body.translated_text: <s>Kṣemitva</s> (safety) is having transcended all grounds for apprehension.

body.text: * bāhyādhyātmikakriyāśūnyatvaṃ niṣkriyatvam // GkT_1.6ab:173
body.translated_text: <s>Niṣkriyatva</s> (inactivity) is being devoid of both external and internal activity.

body.text: * samastacintārahitatvaṃ vītaśokatvam ity etāni lakṣaṇāny asya yogasyātyantotkṛṣṭatvapratipādanārtham uktāni // GkT_1.6ab:174
body.translated_text: <s>Vītaśokatva</s> (freedom from sorrow) is being free from all anxiety. These characteristics have been stated for the purpose of demonstrating the supremely exalted nature of this <s>yoga</s>.

body.text: * pañcamaṃ lābham āha siddhiś ca iti // GkT_1.6ab:175
body.translated_text: He states the fifth <s>lābha</s>: "and <s>siddhi</s> (attainment)."

body.text: * siddhiḥ pūrvavyākhyātā // GkT_1.6ab:176
body.translated_text: <s>Siddhi</s> has been explained previously.

body.text: * sānumānād apy avagamyate // GkT_1.6ab:177
body.translated_text: It is also understood through inference.

body.text: * nirupacaritā muktātmānaḥ paramaiśvaryopetāḥ puruṣatve sati samastaduḥkhabījarahitatvān maheśvaravat // GkT_1.6ab:178
body.translated_text: In the literal sense, liberated souls (<s>muktātman</s>) possess supreme sovereignty (<s>paramaiśvarya</s>), because while possessing the nature of <s>puruṣa</s> (personhood), they are devoid of all seeds of suffering, like <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord). // GkT_1.6ab:178

body.text: * parābhipretā muktātmānaḥ paramaiśvaryavikalatvād asmadādivad iti // GkT_1.6ab:179
body.translated_text: In the other's intended sense, liberated souls (<s>muktātman</s>) are incomplete in supreme sovereignty (<s>paramaiśvarya</s>), like us and others. // GkT_1.6ab:179

body.text: * cakāro nyūnādhikavyavacchedasūcakaḥ // GkT_1.6ab:180
body.translated_text: The particle 'ca' indicates the exclusion of anything less or more. // GkT_1.6ab:180

body.text: * pañcamīti lābhānāṃ pañcatvopasaṃhārārtham iti // GkT_1.6ab:181
body.translated_text: 'Five' (<s>pañcamī</s>) is for the purpose of summarizing the attainments (<s>lābha</s>) as fivefold. // GkT_1.6ab:181

body.text: * athaite lābhāḥ kiṃ deśaniyamena prāptavyā yathā brahmacārigṛhasthavānaprasthabhikṣubhir vidyāprajātayogākhyā lābhāḥ kiṃ vā deśāniyamenāpi pañcaviṃśatitattvajñena kaivalyavad iti // GkT_1.6ab:182
body.translated_text: Now, are these attainments (<s>lābha</s>) to be obtained through restriction of place (<s>deśaniyama</s>), just as the attainments called knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), progeny (<s>prajā</s>), and union (<s>yoga</s>) are obtained by the celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>), householder (<s>gṛhastha</s>), forest-dweller (<s>vānaprastha</s>), and renunciant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) respectively? Or are they obtained without restriction of place, like the liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) attained by one who knows the twenty-five principles (<s>tattva</s>)? // GkT_1.6ab:182

body.text: * ucyate // GkT_1.6ab:183
body.translated_text: It is said: // GkT_1.6ab:183

body.text: * deśaniyamena // GkT_1.6ab:184
body.translated_text: Through restriction of place (<s>deśaniyama</s>). // GkT_1.6ab:184

body.text: * yatas tadartham idam āha // GkT_1.6ab:185]
body.translated_text: Since, for that purpose, he states: // GkT_1.6ab:185]

body.text: gurujanaguhādeśaḥ śmaśānaṃ rudra eva ca // Gk_1.6
body.translated_text: The <s>guru</s> (teacher), <s>jana</s> (people), <s>guhā</s> (cave) are the places (<s>deśa</s>); the cremation ground (<s>śmaśāna</s>) and <s>Rudra</s> himself. // Gk_1.6

body.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: * ārṣatvād vā yathāśrute 'py adoṣaḥ // GkT_1.6cd:1
children.translated_text: Or, due to it being a sacred composition (<s>ārṣa</s>), there is no fault even as heard. // GkT_1.6cd:1

children.text: * guruḥ pūrvoktas tadājñayāvatiṣṭhamānas tadāśrito bhavati yathā grāmaṇyam āśrito grāma iti // GkT_1.6cd:2
children.translated_text: The <s>guru</s> (teacher) is the one previously mentioned; one who abides by his command, being dependent on him, is like a village dependent on a village headman (<s>grāmaṇī</s>). // GkT_1.6cd:2

children.text: * tatrādidharmāvasthasya tāvadāyatane vāsa ityatrāyatanaśabdo gurāv eva draṣṭavyo liṅgakartetyādijñāpakādupacārād vā pañcaśabdavat // GkT_1.6cd:3
children.translated_text: There, for one in the first stage of <s>dharma</s> (religious practice), in the expression 'dwelling in the abode' (<s>āyatane vāsa</s>), the word <s>āyatana</s> (abode) should be understood as referring to the <s>guru</s> alone, either through indication from expressions like 'the maker of the mark' (<s>liṅgakartā</s>), or by figurative usage like the five terms. // GkT_1.6cd:3

children.text: * yadyapyāyatanasūtre pratiṣedhaḥ śrūyate tathāpi deśaprastāve gururabhipreta evācāryo loka ityādi jñāpakābhyanujñānāt // GkT_1.6cd:4
children.translated_text: Although prohibition is heard in the <s>āyatana</s>-<s>sūtra</s>, nevertheless in the context of places (<s>deśa</s>), the <s>guru</s> is indeed intended, because of the permission granted by indicatory statements such as 'the teacher is the world' (<s>ācāryo loka</s>). // GkT_1.6cd:4

children.text: * ata eva gūḍhavratopadeśādāyatane vāsa ityatrāyatanaśabdo jane vivakṣito maryādayāyatanāditi kṛtvā baddhasya rudrasya hi śivāyatanavāsānupapatteḥ // GkT_1.6cd:5
children.translated_text: For this very reason, due to the teaching of the secret observance (<s>gūḍhavrata</s>), in 'dwelling in the abode' (<s>āyatane vāsa</s>), the word <s>āyatana</s> is intended to mean 'among people' (<s>jana</s>), taking it as 'from the abode by convention' (<s>maryādayā āyatanāt</s>), because for one who is bound, dwelling in the abode of <s>Śiva</s> for <s>Rudra</s> is impossible. // GkT_1.6cd:5

children.text: * yadāpi vāsastadāpi janādhīna evetyato dvitīyāvasthasya jana eva deśaḥ // GkT_1.6cd:6
children.translated_text: Even when there is dwelling (<s>vāsa</s>), it is indeed dependent on people (<s>jana</s>); therefore, for one in the second stage, people (<s>jana</s>) alone is the place (<s>deśa</s>). // GkT_1.6cd:6

children.text: * janaśabdenātra dharmādharmajananādhikṛtā varṇāśramino 'bhidhīyanta iti // GkT_1.6cd:7
children.translated_text: By the word <s>jana</s> (people) here, those of the <s>varṇāśrama</s> (caste and life-stage system) who are authorities on the generation of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) are denoted. // GkT_1.6cd:7

children.text: * tṛtīyāvasthasya guhā deśaḥ // GkT_1.6cd:8
children.translated_text: For one in the third stage, a cave (<s>guhā</s>) is the place (<s>deśa</s>). // GkT_1.6cd:8

children.text: * guhāgrahaṇaṃ sūtrārthopalakṣaṇārtham ataḥ śūnyāgāraguhayoranyataraṃ vyāsaṅgādidoṣavarjitaṃ yatprāpyate tatra vastavyam // GkT_1.6cd:9
children.translated_text: The mention of 'cave' (<s>guhā</s>) is for the purpose of indicating the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> by way of example; therefore, one should dwell in whichever of an empty house (<s>śūnyāgāra</s>) or a cave (<s>guhā</s>) is obtained that is free from the fault of attachment (<s>vyāsaṅga</s>) and so forth. // GkT_1.6cd:9

children.text: * deśagrahaṇaṃ tatrāvasthānamātreṇa guhāyā deśatvajñāpanārthaṃ na tu gurujanavat tadāyattatveneti // GkT_1.6cd:10
children.translated_text: The mention of 'place' (<s>deśa</s>) there is for the purpose of indicating that the cave functions as a place merely by staying there, and not in the sense of being dependent on it as with the <s>guru</s> and <s>jana</s> (people). // GkT_1.6cd:10

children.text: * caturthāvasthasya śmaśānadeśaḥ // GkT_1.6cd:11
children.translated_text: For one in the fourth stage, the cremation ground (<s>śmaśāna</s>) is the place (<s>deśa</s>). // GkT_1.6cd:11

children.text: * śmaśānaṃ ca prasiddhameva grāhyam // GkT_1.6cd:12
children.translated_text: The cremation ground (<s>śmaśāna</s>) is to be understood in its well-known sense. // GkT_1.6cd:12

children.text: * tasya ca na guhāvaddeśatvaṃ kiṃ tv ā dehapātāt tatraivānirgacchatā stheyam ityayaṃ viśeṣaḥ // GkT_1.6cd:13
children.translated_text: And its designation as a place (<s>deśa</s>) is not like that of the cave (<s>guhā</s>); rather, the distinction is that one must remain there without departing, until the fall of the body (<s>dehapāta</s>). // GkT_1.6cd:13

children.text: * pañcamāvasthasya deśo rudraḥ // GkT_1.6cd:14
children.translated_text: For one in the fifth stage, the place (<s>deśa</s>) is <s>Rudra</s>. // GkT_1.6cd:14

children.text: * rudro bhagavānmaheśvaraḥ // GkT_1.6cd:15
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> is the Blessed Lord <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord). // GkT_1.6cd:15

children.text: * prāgapi rudrāyattatvāt sādhakasya rudro'styeva deśastathāpi prāganyavyapadeśo 'pyasti sāmprataṃ punaḥ śarīrādirahitasya sarvadeśavikalatvād avadhāraṇaṃ karoti rudra eveti // GkT_1.6cd:16
children.translated_text: Even before, <s>Rudra</s> is indeed the place for the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) due to dependence on <s>Rudra</s>; nevertheless, previously there was also designation by other terms, but now, for one devoid of body and so forth, since all other places are inapplicable, he makes the restriction: '<s>Rudra</s> alone.' // GkT_1.6cd:16

children.text: * caśabdo nyūnādhikavyavacchedaka iti // GkT_1.6cd:17
children.translated_text: The particle 'ca' excludes anything less or more. // GkT_1.6cd:17

children.text: * atha kimetaddeśāvasthitimātreṇaivaite lābhāḥ prāpyante kalpavṛkṣadeśāvasthitivat // GkT_1.6cd:18
children.translated_text: Now, are these attainments (<s>lābha</s>) obtained merely by staying in these places (<s>deśa</s>), like staying in the place of a wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>)? // GkT_1.6cd:18

children.text: * ucyate // GkT_1.6cd:19
children.translated_text: It is said: // GkT_1.6cd:19

children.text: * na // GkT_1.6cd:20
children.translated_text: No. // GkT_1.6cd:20

children.text: * kiṃ tarhi deśabhedavadupāyabhedo 'pyasti // GkT_1.6cd:21
children.translated_text: What then? Just as there is differentiation of places (<s>deśabheda</s>), there is also differentiation of means (<s>upāyabheda</s>). // GkT_1.6cd:21

children.text: * yatas tatpratipādanārtham āha // GkT_1.6cd:22]
children.translated_text: Since, for the purpose of explaining that, he states: // GkT_1.6cd:22]

body.translated_text: [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: vāsaścaryā japadhyānaṃ sadārudrasmṛtistathā /
children.translated_text: Dwelling (<s>vāsa</s>), conduct (<s>caryā</s>), recitation (<s>japa</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and constant remembrance of <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: prasādaścaiva lābhānāmupāyāḥ pañca niścitāḥ // Gk_1.7
children.translated_text: and grace (<s>prasāda</s>) — these are determined as the five means (<s>upāya</s>) of the attainments (<s>lābha</s>). // Gk_1.7

body.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: * grahaṇadhāraṇohāpohavijñānavacanakriyāyathānyāyābhiniveśānāṃ vāsa iti saṃjñā tāntrikī śiṣṭaiḥ kṛtā // GkT_1.7:1
children.translated_text: The technical designation (<s>saṃjñā tāntrikī</s>) '<s>vāsa</s>' (dwelling/study) has been established by the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) for the [eight components]: apprehension (<s>grahaṇa</s>), retention (<s>dhāraṇa</s>), reasoning (<s>ūha</s>), refutation (<s>apoha</s>), discernment (<s>vijñāna</s>), exposition (<s>vacana</s>), practice (<s>kriyā</s>), and proper application (<s>yathānyāyābhiniveśa</s>). // GkT_1.7:1

children.text: * tatra sakṛduccāritavākyasya samyagarthapratipattisāmarthyaṃ grahaṇam // GkT_1.7:2
children.translated_text: Among these, <s>grahaṇa</s> (apprehension) is the capacity for correct understanding of the meaning of a statement uttered only once. // GkT_1.7:2

children.text: * gṛhītasya cirakālavyavadhāne'pi smaraṇasāmarthyaṃ dhāraṇam // GkT_1.7:3
children.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇa</s> (retention) is the capacity to remember what has been apprehended even after a long interval of time. // GkT_1.7:3

children.text: * ekadeśaśravaṇāt tannyāyenāpūrvārthapratipattisāmarthyamūhaḥ // GkT_1.7:4
children.translated_text: <s>Ūha</s> (reasoning) is the capacity for understanding a previously unknown meaning by that same method from hearing only a part. // GkT_1.7:4

children.text: * ācāryadeśīyairuktārthānāṃ yuktāyuktapravibhāgena pratipattityāgasāmarthyam apohaḥ // GkT_1.7:5
children.translated_text: <s>Apoha</s> (refutation) is the capacity for accepting or rejecting the meanings stated by fellow students through discrimination of what is valid and what is invalid. // GkT_1.7:5

children.text: * śrutasyārthasyānekadhāvicāraṇe parapratipādane ca sāmarthyaṃ vijñānam // GkT_1.7:6
children.translated_text: <s>Vijñāna</s> (discernment) is the capacity for examining the meaning of what has been heard in multiple ways and for communicating it to others. // GkT_1.7:6

children.text: * vyāhatapunaruktādidoṣarahitaṃ vākyaṃ vacanam // GkT_1.7:7
children.translated_text: <s>Vacana</s> (exposition) is a statement free from faults such as contradiction and redundancy. // GkT_1.7:7

children.text: * nirduṣṭaśabdoccāraṇenācāryaṃ paritoṣayato mithyājñānamalanivṛttau vidyābhivyaktir bhavati // GkT_1.7:8
children.translated_text: Through faultless utterance of words, by satisfying the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), when the impurity of false knowledge (<s>mithyājñānamala</s>) is removed, the manifestation of true knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) occurs. // GkT_1.7:8

children.text: * tathotthānapratyutthānādikā gurau paricaryā kriyetyuktā // GkT_1.7:9
children.translated_text: Similarly, service to the <s>guru</s> (teacher) such as rising, standing up to greet, and the like, is called <s>kriyā</s> (practice). // GkT_1.7:9

children.text: * yuktyāpi pūrvottarāviruddhaśāstrārthaparyālocane tadarthānuṣṭhānārthamatiyatno yathā nyāyābhiniveśaḥ // GkT_1.7:10
children.translated_text: <s>Yathānyāyābhiniveśa</s> (proper application) is the diligent intellectual effort toward the investigation of the non-contradictory meaning of scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) in its earlier and later portions, with the purpose of practicing that meaning, through reasoning (<s>yukti</s>) as well. // GkT_1.7:10

children.text: * tathā coktam /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said:

children.text: * pūrvottarāvirodhena vākyārthaṃ hy avicālitam /
children.translated_text: One who investigates the meaning of statements through reasoning (<s>tarka</s>), consistently and without contradiction between earlier and later portions,

children.text: * yastarkeṇānusaṃdhatte sa dharmaṃ veda netaraḥ // GkT_1.7:11
children.translated_text: he knows <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), and no other. // GkT_1.7:11

children.text: * dharmasyopāyaḥ caryā // GkT_1.7:12
children.translated_text: <s>Caryā</s> (conduct) is the means (<s>upāya</s>) for <s>dharma</s> (merit). // GkT_1.7:12

children.text: * bhasmasnānādir mūḍhāntaḥ kriyāsamūhaścaryetyucyate // GkT_1.7:13
children.translated_text: The collection of actions beginning with ash-bathing (<s>bhasmasnāna</s>) and ending with acting as if deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>) is called <s>caryā</s> (conduct). // GkT_1.7:13

children.text: * sā ca tryaṅgā dānayāgatāpāṅgeti // GkT_1.7:14
children.translated_text: And it has three limbs (<s>aṅga</s>): giving (<s>dāna</s>), sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), and austerity (<s>tāpa</s>). // GkT_1.7:14

children.text: * pañcasu pavitreṣvāvartyamāneṣu daśabhirnamaskāraiḥ parameśvarāyātmasamarpaṇaṃ dānam // GkT_1.7:15
children.translated_text: While the five purificatory mantras (<s>pavitra</s>) are being recited, the offering of oneself (<s>ātmasamarpaṇa</s>) to the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) with ten salutations (<s>namaskāra</s>) is <s>dāna</s> (giving). // GkT_1.7:15

children.text: * tadevātidānam anāvṛttiphalatvāt // GkT_1.7:16
children.translated_text: That itself is supreme giving (<s>atidāna</s>), because its fruit is non-return (<s>anāvṛtti</s>). // GkT_1.7:16

children.text: * anyattu kudānam āvṛttiphalatvād iti // GkT_1.7:17
children.translated_text: But other giving is inferior giving (<s>kudāna</s>), because its fruit involves return (<s>āvṛtti</s>). // GkT_1.7:17

children.text: * parameśvaraniyogābhisaṃdhinā bhasmasnānādikriyāṇāṃ yathāvihitakaraṇaṃ yāgaḥ // GkT_1.7:18
children.translated_text: <s>Yāga</s> (sacrifice) is the performance of actions such as ash-bathing (<s>bhasmasnāna</s>) and the like as prescribed, with the intention directed toward the command of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). // GkT_1.7:18

children.text: * sa evātiyāgo 'nyastu kuyāgaḥ pūrvoktahetudvayāt // GkT_1.7:19
children.translated_text: That itself is supreme sacrifice (<s>atiyāga</s>); but other sacrifice is false sacrifice (<s>kuyāga</s>), for the two reasons stated previously. // GkT_1.7:19

children.text: * svavidhyabhiniviṣṭasyaiva trividhaduḥkhopanipāte sati anupāyataḥ pratīkāramakurvataḥ sahiṣṇutvaṃ tāpaḥ // GkT_1.7:20
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpa</s> (austerity) is patient endurance (<s>sahiṣṇutva</s>) when the threefold suffering (<s>trividhaduḥkha</s>) befalls one who is devoted to his own discipline (<s>svavidyā</s>), without resorting to remedies through improper means. // GkT_1.7:20

children.text: * sa evātitāpo'nyattu kutāpa iti // GkT_1.7:21
children.translated_text: That itself is supreme austerity (<s>atitāpa</s>); but other austerity is false austerity (<s>kutāpa</s>). // GkT_1.7:21

children.text: * sā tryaṅgāpi caryā dvividhā vrataṃ dvārāṇi ceti // GkT_1.7:22
children.translated_text: That <s>caryā</s> (conduct), though having three limbs, is twofold: observance (<s>vrata</s>) and gates (<s>dvāra</s>). // GkT_1.7:22

children.text: * tatra snānaśayanopahārajapapradakṣiṇāni vratam dharmaniṣpattyadharmocchedārthaṃ prādhānyena kriyamāṇatvāt // GkT_1.7:23
children.translated_text: Among these, bathing (<s>snāna</s>), lying on the ground (<s>śayana</s>), offering (<s>upahāra</s>), recitation (<s>japa</s>), and circumambulation (<s>pradakṣiṇā</s>) constitute the observance (<s>vrata</s>), because they are performed principally for the accomplishment of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and the destruction of <s>adharma</s> (demerit). // GkT_1.7:23

children.text: * dvārāṇi tu krāthanaspandanamandanaśṛṅgāraṇāpitatkaraṇāpi tadbhāṣaṇāni // GkT_1.7:24
children.translated_text: The gates (<s>dvāra</s>), however, are: acting disgracefully (<s>krāthana</s>), trembling (<s>spandana</s>), acting ornamentally (<s>mandana</s>), acting amourously (<s>śṛṅgāraṇa</s>), acting as if doing that (<s>apitatkaraṇa</s>), and speaking as if that (<s>apitatbhāṣaṇa</s>). // GkT_1.7:24

children.text: * apamānaparibhavaparivādaniṣpādanadvāreṇa pūrvotpannayor dharmādharmayor āyavyayanimittatvāditi kramaḥ svarūpaṃ caiṣāṃ bhāṣya eva prapañcitam // GkT_1.7:25
children.translated_text: Through the gate of producing disrespect (<s>apamāna</s>), humiliation (<s>paribhava</s>), and censure (<s>parivāda</s>), these serve as the cause of income and expenditure regarding the <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) previously accumulated — this is the sequence. The nature of these has been elaborated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) itself. // GkT_1.7:25

children.text: * tadanusāreṇa śiṣyahitārthaṃ mayāpi leśataḥ pradarśyate // GkT_1.7:26
children.translated_text: Following that, for the benefit of the student (<s>śiṣya</s>), it is briefly demonstrated by me as well. // GkT_1.7:26

children.text: * prāgādityodayāt ghaṭikādvayaṃ pūrvāhṇasaṃdhyā // GkT_1.7:27
children.translated_text: Two <s>ghaṭikā</s>s (48 minutes) before sunrise is the morning twilight junction (<s>pūrvāhṇasaṃdhyā</s>). // GkT_1.7:27

children.text: * sā tridevatā // GkT_1.7:28
children.translated_text: It has three deities (<s>tridevatā</s>). // GkT_1.7:28

children.text: * prathamā brāhmī madhyamā vaiṣṇavī antyā raudrī // GkT_1.7:29
children.translated_text: The first is of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>brāhmī</s>), the middle is of <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>vaiṣṇavī</s>), and the last is of <s>Rudra</s> (<s>raudrī</s>). // GkT_1.7:29

children.text: * tatra pūrvasaṃdhyayoḥ śaucaṃ kṛtvā bhasma saṃskartavyam // GkT_1.7:30
children.translated_text: There, during the two twilight junctions (<s>saṃdhyā</s>), having performed purification (<s>śauca</s>), the ash (<s>bhasma</s>) should be consecrated. // GkT_1.7:30

children.text: * kartṛkārakādidoṣarahitaṃ śuklādiguṇayuktaṃ ca bhasmārjitaṃ śivadakṣiṇamūrtau mantraiḥ saṃskṛtya pradakṣiṇaṃ ca dattvā sūryarūpiṇaṃ bhagavantaṃ locanatrayeṇa prasannadṛṣṭyā bhasma paśyantaṃ dhyāyet // GkT_1.7:31
children.translated_text: Having procured ash (<s>bhasma</s>) that is free from faults of agent and instrument and endowed with qualities such as whiteness, having consecrated it with <s>mantras</s> at the <s>Śiva</s> <s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti</s> (south-facing form), and having offered circumambulation (<s>pradakṣiṇa</s>), one should meditate on the Blessed Lord in the form of the Sun (<s>Sūrya</s>), gazing upon the ash with three eyes (<s>locanātraya</s>) with a gracious glance (<s>prasannadṛṣṭi</s>). // GkT_1.7:31

children.text: * tadanu cācāryāya śivatattvānurañjitadṛṣṭaye jyeṣṭhabhrātre vā nivedayet // GkT_1.7:32
children.translated_text: After that, one should present it to the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) — one whose vision is imbued with the reality of <s>Śiva</s> (<s>śivatattva</s>) — or to the elder brother (<s>jyeṣṭhabhrātṛ</s>). // GkT_1.7:32

children.text: * tadanv ekānte śucau pradeśe jantusthāvarahīne pañca pavitrāṇyāvartayataiva stheyaṃ raudrasavanaṃ yāvattato bhagavantaṃ praṇamya tvadājñāṃ karomītyabhisaṃdhāya japannaivāpādatalamastakaṃ yāvat prabhūtena bhasmanāṅgaṃ pratyaṅgaṃ ca prayatnātiśayena nighṛṣya nighṛṣya snānamācared ityevaṃ madhyāhnāparāhṇasaṃdhyayor apīti // GkT_1.7:33
children.translated_text: After that, in a secluded, clean spot free from living creatures and immovable objects, while reciting the five purificatory mantras (<s>pavitra</s>), one should remain until the <s>Raudra</s> oblation (<s>raudrasavana</s>); then, having bowed to the Blessed Lord, resolving 'I perform Your command,' while reciting (<s>japa</s>), one should rub abundantly with ash (<s>bhasma</s>) each limb and sub-limb from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head, with utmost effort, rubbing thoroughly, and thus perform the bath (<s>snāna</s>) — and likewise for the midday and afternoon twilight junctions (<s>saṃdhyā</s>). // GkT_1.7:33

children.text: * etāvadatra viśiṣyate // GkT_1.7:34
children.translated_text: This much is the distinguishing feature here. // GkT_1.7:34

children.text: * madhyāhne prathamā brāhmī madhye mastakoparisthite ravau raudrī tadante vaiṣṇavī arkāstasamayottaratra prathamā raudrī tadanu vaiṣṇavī tadante brāhmī ceti // GkT_1.7:35
children.translated_text: At midday, the first is of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>brāhmī</s>); in the middle, when the sun is directly overhead, is of <s>Rudra</s> (<s>raudrī</s>); at the end of that, of <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>vaiṣṇavī</s>). After sunset, the first is of <s>Rudra</s> (<s>raudrī</s>), then of <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>vaiṣṇavī</s>), and at the end, of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>brāhmī</s>). // GkT_1.7:35

children.text: * sarvatra raudrasavanameva snānakālaḥ // GkT_1.7:36
children.translated_text: In all cases, the <s>Raudra</s> oblation (<s>raudrasavana</s>) alone is the time for bathing (<s>snāna</s>). // GkT_1.7:36

children.text: * evaṃ snānaṃ nirvartya japann evāyatanaṃ gatvā śivaṃ bhaktyatiśayena praṇamya snānaṃ nivedya ca śanairgarbhagṛhaṃ praviśet // GkT_1.7:37
children.translated_text: Having thus completed the bath, [the practitioner], while reciting (<s>japa</s>), should go to the temple (<s>āyatana</s>), bow to <s>Śiva</s> with supreme devotion, announce [the completion of] the bath, and slowly enter the inner sanctum (<s>garbhagṛha</s>). (GkT 1.7:37)

children.text: * tadanu mūrtidakṣiṇe deśe jānunī pātayitvā hṛdi cāñjaliṃ baddhvā mūrtisthaṃ sākṣādiva śivaṃ paśyan yadyanivṛttapratyāhārastadā gatamātra eva hasitaṃ kuryādityeke // GkT_1.7:38
children.translated_text: Then, on the right side of the image, having placed [both] knees [on the ground] and having joined the palms at the heart, gazing at <s>Śiva</s> present in the image as if directly [before him] — if [the practitioner] has not yet achieved <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses), then immediately upon arriving he should perform laughter — so say some [commentators]. (GkT 1.7:38)

children.text: * vayaṃ tu paśyāmo'bhigamya ca yatpūrvaṃ japatītyādi bhāṣyasyārtho yadi vicāryate tadāvaśyaṃ gatvā saṃyatātmanottarābhimukhena pratyāhāraviśeṣārthaṃ japtavyaṃ japtvā tu śivadhyānāsakta evāṭṭahāsaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kuryāt // GkT_1.7:39
children.translated_text: But we observe [the following]: if the meaning of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>'s [statement] 'having approached, he first recites' and so on is carefully considered, then necessarily, having gone, with a controlled self, facing north, he should recite for the specific purpose of <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense-withdrawal); and having recited, while remaining absorbed in meditation on <s>Śiva</s>, he should perform loud laughter (<s>aṭṭahāsa</s>) again and again. (GkT 1.7:39)

children.text: * tadanu gītam ārabhya gāyann evottiṣṭhet // GkT_1.7:40
children.translated_text: Then, commencing a song (<s>gīta</s>), he should rise up while singing. (GkT 1.7:40)

children.text: * tato gītasahitameva nṛtyaṃ kuryāt // GkT_1.7:41
children.translated_text: Then he should perform dance (<s>nṛtya</s>) together with song. (GkT 1.7:41)

children.text: * tatrādau gītaṃ parisamāpya paścānnṛtyaṃ samāpayet // GkT_1.7:42
children.translated_text: Therein, having first completed the song, he should afterward conclude the dance. (GkT 1.7:42)

children.text: * tadanu pūrvoktavidhinopaviśya śivaṃ dhyāyanneva huḍukkāraṃ kṛtvā namaskāraṃ kuryāttadanu japamiti // GkT_1.7:43
children.translated_text: Then, sitting down according to the previously stated procedure, while meditating on <s>Śiva</s>, having made the <s>huḍukkāra</s> (bellowing sound), he should make obeisance (<s>namaskāra</s>); then [perform] <s>japa</s> (recitation). (GkT 1.7:43)

children.text: * atra japanamaskārau mānasāv eva nṛtyaṃ kāyikameva hasitagītahuḍukkārā vācikā eveti niyama iṣṭaḥ // GkT_1.7:44
children.translated_text: Here the desired rule is: <s>japa</s> (recitation) and <s>namaskāra</s> (obeisance) are mental only; dance is bodily only; laughter, song, and <s>huḍukkāra</s> are vocal only. (GkT 1.7:44)

children.text: * tatra dīrghocchvāsatrayaṃ yāvaddhasitaṃ daṇḍakatrirāvartanaṃ yāvadgītanṛtye gambhīrahuḍukkāratrayaṃ ṣaṣṭi namaskārān pañcapavitrāṇāṃ trir āvartanaṃ kuryādityāha bhagavānācāryaḥ svāmī mama yenāhamajñānārṇavāduttāritaḥ // GkT_1.7:45
children.translated_text: Therein, laughter [should be performed] for the duration of three long exhalations; song and dance [should each last] for three repetitions of the <s>daṇḍaka</s> [verse]; three deep <s>huḍukkāras</s>; sixty obeisances; and the five <s>pavitras</s> (purifying mantras) should be repeated three times — so says the blessed teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), my lord, by whom I was rescued from the ocean of ignorance. (GkT 1.7:45)

children.text: * ṭīkākārāstu sarvam ā paritoṣāt kartavyamityevaṃ pratipannāḥ // GkT_1.7:46
children.translated_text: But the commentators (<s>ṭīkākāras</s>) have understood that all [these practices] should be performed to [the point of] satisfaction. (GkT 1.7:46)

children.text: * tadevaṃ nirvartyopahāraṃ dhyāyannīśaṃ hasitagītanṛtyahuḍukkāranamaskārajapyaiḥ ṣaḍaṅgopahāraṃ bhagavanmahādeva yuṣmadanujñayā nirvartitavān aham avabhṛthasnānaṃ ca kariṣyāmītyevaṃ nivedayet // GkT_1.7:47
children.translated_text: Thus, having completed the offering (<s>upahāra</s>), while meditating on the Lord, [the practitioner] should announce through laughter, song, dance, <s>huḍukkāra</s>, obeisance, and <s>japa</s> — [constituting] the sixfold offering: 'O blessed <s>Mahādeva</s>, by your permission I have completed [the offering], and I shall now perform the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding) bath.' (GkT 1.7:47)

children.text: * tato niṣkramyeśaṃ praṇamya praṇāmāntaṃ pradakṣiṇatrayaṃ japann eva śanaiḥ kuryāt // GkT_1.7:48
children.translated_text: Then, going out, bowing to the Lord, he should slowly perform three circumambulations ending with a prostration, while reciting. (GkT 1.7:48)

children.text: * tato'vabhṛthasnānaṃ kṛtvā bhagavaṃllakulīśādīn rāśīkarāntāṃśca tīrthakarānanukrameṇa yathāvadbhaktyā namaskuryāt tadanu pradakṣiṇamekamiti // GkT_1.7:49
children.translated_text: Then, having performed the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding) bath, he should bow with devotion in proper sequence to the blessed <s>Lakulīśa</s> and the other <s>tīrthakaras</s> (lineage masters) up to and including the <s>Rāśīkaras</s> (lineage-holders); then one circumambulation. (GkT 1.7:49)

children.text: * anyadā tu yāvadicchaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ japann eva kuryāt pañcamantrajapastu kevalo'pi dharmahetur iti // GkT_1.7:50
children.translated_text: At other times, he should perform circumambulations as many as desired, while reciting. The <s>pañcamantra</s>-<s>japa</s> (recitation of the five mantras) alone, even by itself, is a cause of <s>dharma</s> (spiritual merit). (GkT 1.7:50)

children.text: * athāyatanasaṃdhinaṃ deśaṃ divā parigṛhītasthāvarādidoṣavarjitatvena suparīkṣitaṃ saṃdhyāvasāne vastrāntādimṛdupavitreṇa vivecya bhasmanaiva śuciṃ kuryāt // GkT_1.7:51
children.translated_text: Then, at the juncture [area] of the temple, [taking] a spot well-examined during the day [to be] free from defects such as [presence of] plants and the like, at the end of twilight, having swept it with a soft cloth-end or the like, he should purify it with sacred ash (<s>bhasman</s>) alone. (GkT 1.7:51)

children.text: * tadanu tatropaviśya vidhyabhiniviṣṭas tāvat tiṣṭhed yāvad atinidrābhibhūtaḥ śrāntaśca bhavati // GkT_1.7:52
children.translated_text: Then, having sat down there, devoted to the ritual procedure, he should remain [seated] until he is overcome by extreme drowsiness and becomes fatigued. (GkT 1.7:52)

children.text: * tataḥ punarutthāya vivecayet // GkT_1.7:53
children.translated_text: Then, rising again, he should sweep [the area again]. (GkT 1.7:53)

children.text: * tadanu mantraiḥ saṃskṛtya bhasma prabhūtaṃ prastaret // GkT_1.7:54
children.translated_text: Then, having consecrated ash with mantras, he should spread it abundantly [on the ground]. (GkT 1.7:54)

children.text: * tatastatra pañca mantrānāvartayanneva svapet punarutthāyānenaiva vidhinā svapedyenāśveva śuddhivṛddhī bhavataḥ // GkT_1.7:55
children.translated_text: Then he should sleep there while repeating the five mantras; rising again, he should sleep by this same procedure — by which purity and [spiritual] growth quickly occur. (GkT 1.7:55)

children.text: * suptasyāpi prāṇātyaye cātigatiḥ syādanyathā vidhibhraṣṭasya saṃsārāpattir eveti // GkT_1.7:56
children.translated_text: Even while sleeping, in the event of death, there would be the supreme destination (<s>atigati</s>); otherwise, for one who has deviated from the procedure, there is only the calamity of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). (GkT 1.7:56)

children.text: * evaṃ prathamāvasthāyāṃ vidhim anuṣṭhāya yadā khalu prāptajñānaḥ prakṣīṇakaluṣaḥ kṛtābhyanujñaśca bhavati tadāvasthāntaraṃ gatvā raṅgavadavasthiteṣu janeṣu madhye naṭavadavasthito vivecya vivecya krāthanādīni kuryāt // GkT_1.7:57
children.translated_text: Thus, having practiced the procedure in the first stage, when indeed [the practitioner] has attained knowledge, has diminished [his] impurities, and has received authorization — then, having passed to the next stage, while people stand as if in an arena [watching], he, standing in their midst like a dancer, should, having swept [the ground] again and again, perform <s>krāthana</s> (feigning sleep) and the other [practices]. (GkT 1.7:57)

children.text: * tatrāsuptasyeva suptaliṅgapradarśanaṃ krāthanaṃ vāyvabhibhūtasyeva śarīrāvayavānāṃ kampanaṃ spandanam upahatapādendriyasyeva gamanaṃ mandanam // GkT_1.7:58
children.translated_text: Therein: <s>krāthana</s> is the display of the signs of sleep while not actually sleeping; <s>spandana</s> (trembling) is the shaking of bodily limbs as if overcome by wind; <s>mandana</s> (limping) is walking as if one's foot-faculty is impaired. (GkT 1.7:58)

children.text: * yauvanasampannāṃ striyamavalokayan kāmukam ivātmānaṃ yair liṅgaiḥ pradarśayati tac chṛṅgāraṇaṃ kāryākāryavivekaśūnyasyeva lokaninditakaraṇam api tatkaraṇaṃ vyāhatāpārthakādiśabdoccāraṇam api tad bhāṣaṇam iti // GkT_1.7:59
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgāraṇa</s> (erotic display) is showing oneself as if amorous while gazing at a woman endowed with youth. Acting [improperly] (<s>tatkaraṇa</s>) is doing what is condemned by the world, as if devoid of the discrimination between what should and should not be done. Speaking [improperly] (<s>tadbhāṣaṇa</s>) is uttering contradictory, meaningless, and other [such] words. (GkT 1.7:59)

children.text: * na caiṣāṃ kramo niyamyate // GkT_1.7:60
children.translated_text: And the sequence of these is not fixed. (GkT 1.7:60)

children.text: * kiṃtvapamānādiniṣpādakatvaṃ yena paribhavaṃ gacched ityupadeśād davāgnitulyatvenāpamānāder iṣṭatamatvād iti // GkT_1.7:61
children.translated_text: But the characteristic of [these practices] is that they produce dishonor (<s>apamāna</s>) and the like — [the purpose being] that [the practitioner] should be subjected to contempt. From the teaching that dishonor and the like are most desired, being like wildfire [that burns impurities]. (GkT 1.7:61)

children.text: * evaṃ tarhi hiṃsāsteyādikaraṇaduṣṭaśabdoccāraṇaprasaṅgo'pi syād apamānādiniṣpādakatvād iti // GkT_1.7:62
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Then there would also be the occasion for uttering wicked words [characteristic of] violence, theft, and the like, since they too produce dishonor. (GkT 1.7:62)

children.text: * nāpi tatkaraṇāpi tadbhāṣaṇo devāśeṣakriyāvyāptāvahiṃsādyavirodhajñāpanārthatvāt krāthanādyārambhasyeti /
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Not even through acting [improperly] or speaking [improperly] [is this the case], because the commencement of <s>krāthana</s> and the rest is for the purpose of making known that non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) and the like are not contradicted by the complete range of activities of a god [i.e., an advanced practitioner].

children.text: * devanityatve kastarhi upāya ityāha japadhyānam iti // GkT_1.7:63
children.translated_text: 'What then is the means for [attaining] the permanent state of a god?' He says: <s>japa</s> (recitation) and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). (GkT 1.7:63)

children.text: * tatra tṛtīyacaturthakasya mantrasyāvartanaṃ japaḥ // GkT_1.7:64
children.translated_text: Therein, <s>japa</s> is the repetition of the third and fourth mantra. (GkT 1.7:64)

children.text: * sa dvividhaḥ pratyāhāraphalaḥ samādhiphalaśceti // GkT_1.7:65
children.translated_text: That [japa] is of two kinds: having <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense-withdrawal) as its fruit, and having <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) as its fruit. (GkT 1.7:65)

children.text: * tatrādyaḥ pratyāhāraphalastanniṣpattau ca kriyamāṇo japaḥ samādhiphala iti // GkT_1.7:66
children.translated_text: Therein, the first has <s>pratyāhāra</s> as its fruit; and <s>japa</s> performed after the attainment of that [pratyāhāra] has <s>samādhi</s> as its fruit. (GkT 1.7:66)

children.text: * nanu cānyāsaktatve kriyamāṇo japaḥ saṃvatsaraśatenāpi na pratyāhāraṃ karotyapi tu doṣameva tasya janayatīti // GkT_1.7:67
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But <s>japa</s> performed while the [mind] is attached to other [objects], even for a hundred years, does not produce <s>pratyāhāra</s>; rather, it generates only a fault [in the practitioner]. (GkT 1.7:67)

children.text: * satyam evametat // GkT_1.7:68
children.translated_text: True, this is indeed so. (GkT 1.7:68)

children.text: * kiṃtu pratyāhāradvaividhyamiheṣṭaṃ parāparabhedāt // GkT_1.7:69
children.translated_text: However, a twofold [classification of] <s>pratyāhāra</s> is intended here, on the basis of the distinction between higher and lower. (GkT 1.7:69)

children.text: * tatrāntaḥkaraṇapūrvako 'paraḥ // GkT_1.7:70
children.translated_text: Therein, the lower [pratyāhāra] is preceded by the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) [i.e., requires mental effort]. (GkT 1.7:70)

children.text: * tatsahitena japena nirmalīkṛtaṃ cittaṃ prayatnanirapekṣamapi brahmaṇyevālātacakravad avatiṣṭhate yadā tadāsau paraḥ pratyāhāro japapūrvaka evāyam ityuktaḥ // GkT_1.7:71
children.translated_text: When the mind, purified by <s>japa</s> accompanied by that [inner organ effort], rests in <s>Brahman</s> alone — like a whirling firebrand [appearing as a circle] — even without [further] effort, then that is the higher <s>pratyāhāra</s>. It is said to be preceded by <s>japa</s> [because japa was its precondition]. (GkT 1.7:71)

children.text: * sa hy anekajanmopārjitaṃ karma lakṣaṇamātreṇa dagdhvā dhyeyatattve cittaṃ stambhanikṣiptāyaḥkīlakavan niścalīkaroti // GkT_1.7:72
children.translated_text: For that [japa], having burned by mere indication [i.e., minimal effort] the <s>karma</s> accumulated over many births, renders the mind motionless upon the reality to be meditated on (<s>dhyeya-tattva</s>) — like an iron nail driven into a post. (GkT 1.7:72)

children.text: * rudratattve sadṛśaścintāpravāho dhyānam // GkT_1.7:73
children.translated_text: <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is an unbroken stream of thought (<s>cintā-pravāha</s>) directed toward the <s>Rudra</s>-reality. (GkT 1.7:73)

children.text: * tad dvividhaṃ japapūrvakaṃ dhāraṇāpūrvakaṃ ca // GkT_1.7:74
children.translated_text: That [dhyāna] is of two kinds: preceded by <s>japa</s>, and preceded by <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration). (GkT 1.7:74)

children.text: * tatra japapūrvakaṃ prasaṅgenaiva pūrvam uktaṃ dhāraṇāpūrvakaṃ tūcyate // GkT_1.7:75
children.translated_text: Therein, [dhyāna] preceded by <s>japa</s> has already been stated incidentally earlier. [Dhyāna] preceded by <s>dhāraṇā</s> is now explained. (GkT 1.7:75)

children.text: * nirālambanaṃ cittamamūḍhasya dhāraṇam // GkT_1.7:76
children.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is [rendering] the mind of one who is undeluded support-less (<s>nirālambana</s>). (GkT 1.7:76)

children.text: * saṃhṛtamūrchādyavasthasyāpi cittaṃ vṛttālābhānnirālambanam astīti tannivṛttyartham amūḍhasyetyuktam // GkT_1.7:77
children.translated_text: Since even one whose consciousness has been withdrawn [into states like] fainting and the like has a support-less mind — due to the non-attainment of [cognitive] activity — therefore, in order to exclude that [state], it is said 'of one who is undeluded.' (GkT 1.7:77)

children.text: * yo vidyānugṛhītayā buddhyā svaṃ cittaṃ nirālambanaṃ karoti so 'mūḍha ityucyate // GkT_1.7:78
children.translated_text: He who, by means of an intellect graced by [proper] knowledge, makes his own mind support-less — he is called 'undeluded.' (GkT 1.7:78)

children.text: * tayā dhāraṇayā nirmalīkṛtaṃ cittaṃ rudratattve sthāpitaṃ sudīrghakālaṃ na cyavata ityanenaiva viśeṣeṇa pūrvadhyānāpekṣayedaṃ dhāraṇāsahitaṃ dhyānaṃ paramityuktaṃ śrīmadbhāṣyakṛtā paramayoginā // GkT_1.7:79
children.translated_text: The mind purified by that <s>dhāraṇā</s>, placed upon the <s>Rudra</s>-reality, does not fall away for a very long time — it is by precisely this distinction, in relation to the former meditation [preceded by japa], that this meditation accompanied by <s>dhāraṇā</s> is said to be supreme — so stated the illustrious author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the supreme yogin. (GkT 1.7:79)

children.text: * yadyapyeva dīkṣāprabhṛti cittaṃ nirmalīkartuṃ na śakyate tathāpi dhānuṣkacitrakarādivad abhyāsārthaṃ sarvāvasthāsu yathāśaktyā dhyānaṃ kartavyaṃ mṛtyukālasyāniścitatvāt // GkT_1.7:80
children.translated_text: Although from the time of initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) onwards, the mind cannot [immediately] be purified [completely], nevertheless — like an archer or a painter — meditation should be practiced for the sake of training in all stages, to the extent of one's ability, since the time of death is uncertain. (GkT 1.7:80)

children.text: * anyathā hi yuddhakāla eva aśvadamananyāyaḥ syāditi // GkT_1.7:81
children.translated_text: Otherwise indeed, it would be like the maxim of taming a horse [only] at the time of battle. (GkT 1.7:81)

children.text: * itthaṃ samyagvidhiṃ jñātvā yastu dhyāyati śaṃkaram /
children.translated_text: Thus, one who, having properly known the procedure, meditates on <s>Śaṃkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)

children.text: * niśādāv ardharātre ca niśānte cācyutavrataḥ // GkT_1.7:82
children.translated_text: at the beginning of the night, at midnight, and at the end of the night, with unswerving vow — (GkT 1.7:82)

children.text: * yāmaṃ yāmaṃ tadarghaṃ yāvacchaktyā divāpi ca /
children.translated_text: for one <s>yāma</s> (watch) [at a time], or its equivalent, as long as ability [permits], and also during the day,

children.text: * saṃtyajyāsaktim anyatra paśyanduḥkhamayaṃ bhavam // GkT_1.7:83
children.translated_text: abandoning attachment to other [objects], seeing worldly existence as full of suffering — (GkT 1.7:83)

children.text: * paraṃ vairāgyamāsthāya laghvāhāro jitendriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: having resorted to supreme dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), eating lightly, with senses conquered,

children.text: * utsāhātiśayaṃ kurvan śuddhotkarṣaṃ vivardhayan // GkT_1.7:84
children.translated_text: cultivating an excess of zeal, increasing pure elevation — (GkT 1.7:84)

children.text: * nairantaryeṇa ṣaṇmāsaṃ brahmahatyādimānapi /
children.translated_text: continuously for six months — even one bearing [the sin of] <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brahmin) —

children.text: * ekaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ vāpi taccittastanmayo bhavet // GkT_1.7:85
children.translated_text: or for one year — [such a practitioner] becomes one whose mind is absorbed in That, becomes one with That. (GkT 1.7:85)

children.text: * sa hatvā duṣkṛtaṃ ghoraṃ rāgādīnāṃ ca pañjaram /
children.translated_text: Having destroyed terrible sin and the cage of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest,

children.text: * paśyatyevākhilaṃ tattvaṃ sarvopādhisamanvitam // GkT_1.7:86
children.translated_text: he directly perceives the entire reality, endowed with all limiting conditions (<s>upādhis</s>). (GkT 1.7:86)

children.text: * sarvasattvādhipaṃ paśyann anantaṃ śivamavyayam /
children.translated_text: Perceiving the lord of all beings — infinite, auspicious (<s>Śiva</s>), imperishable —

children.text: * yo na pāśupatādanyair yogīśairapi dṛśyate // GkT_1.7:87
children.translated_text: who is not seen even by the lords of yogins other than those of the <s>Pāśupata</s> [tradition]. (GkT 1.7:87)

children.text: * taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaiśvaryaṃ labdhvā syānnirbhayaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Having seen Him, having obtained supreme lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>), one would be forever fearless.

children.text: * ajñātvāpi vidhānaṃ yasteṣu kāleṣu suvrataḥ // GkT_1.7:88
children.translated_text: Even one who does not know the [ritual] procedure, if [he is] of good vow during those times — (GkT 1.7:88)

children.text: * sadbhaktyutsāhavairāgyair nityaṃ dhyāyati śaṃkaram /
children.translated_text: With true devotion, zeal, and dispassion, [he who] constantly meditates on <s>Śaṃkara</s>,

children.text: * tasyāpīśaḥ prasannastāṃ siddhiṃ dadyādanuttamām // GkT_1.7:89
children.translated_text: to him also the Lord, being pleased, would grant that unsurpassed <s>siddhi</s> (attainment).

children.text: * yāṃ prāpya tyaktasaṃsāraḥ svatantraḥ śivavadbhavet /
children.translated_text: Having attained which, one who has abandoned <s>saṃsāra</s> becomes independent, like <s>Śiva</s> himself,

children.text: * dhyāyanneva tamīśānaṃ yadi prāṇān vimuñcati // GkT_1.7:90
children.translated_text: if while meditating on that very <s>Īśāna</s> (Lord), one releases the vital breaths,

children.text: * tasya dehāntakāle vai dadyādīśaḥ parāṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: at the time of the body's end, the Lord indeed would grant him the supreme destination.

children.text: * abbhakṣā vāyubhakṣāśca ye cātyugratapaścarāḥ // GkT_1.7:91
children.translated_text: Those who subsist on water, those who subsist on air, and those who practice extremely fierce austerities,

children.text: * kṣityādīnāṃ ca dātāro yajñānuṣṭhāyinaśca ye /
children.translated_text: and those who are givers of land and such, and those who perform sacrifices —

children.text: * saṃvatsarasahasreṇa yāṃ siddhiṃ prāpnuvanti te // GkT_1.7:92
children.translated_text: the <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) which they attain in a thousand years,

children.text: * tāṃ prāpnotyardhayāmena japadhyāne rato yatiḥ /
children.translated_text: an ascetic devoted to <s>japa</s> (recitation) and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) attains that in half a <s>yāma</s> (watch, approximately one and a half hours).

children.text: * jñātvaivaṃ yogamāhātmyaṃ dehādeḥ sthityaniścayam // GkT_1.7:93
children.translated_text: Having thus known the greatness of <s>yoga</s> and the uncertainty of the continuance of the body and the like,

children.text: * duḥkhārṇavaṃ ca saṃsāraṃ na kuryādanyathā matim /
children.translated_text: and [knowing] <s>saṃsāra</s> to be an ocean of suffering, one should not form any other resolve.

children.text: * śarīraṃ dhriyate yāvadyāvadbuddhirna hīyate // GkT_1.7:94
children.translated_text: As long as the body is sustained, as long as the intellect is not diminished,

children.text: * tāvaddhyānaṃ japaṃ caiva yāvacchaktyā samabhyaset /
children.translated_text: so long should one practice <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>japa</s> (recitation) to the utmost of one's ability.

children.text: * iṣṭaṃ dravyaṃ yathā naṣṭaṃ kaściddhyāyatyaharniśam /
children.translated_text: Just as someone meditates day and night on a beloved object that has been lost,

children.text: * tadvadvāgādyasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ śivaṃ dhyāyed anālasaḥ // GkT_1.7:95
children.translated_text: so too should one, without laziness, meditate on <s>Śiva</s>, who is untouched by speech and the other [senses].

children.text: * vivakṣor vāgviśuddhaḥ prāg yadvaccetasi bhāsate /
children.translated_text: Just as for one who wishes to speak, the word shines forth in the mind in its purity before [utterance],

children.text: * tadvattaṃ praṇidhānena divā rātrau ca cintayet // GkT_1.7:96
children.translated_text: so too should one contemplate Him with focused intention, day and night.

children.text: * guṇairdharmairviśiṣṭaṃ vā bhāvayitvāśu niścitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having contemplated [Him] as distinguished by qualities and attributes, once one is firmly resolved,

children.text: * paścāttaṃ kevalaṃ dhyāyedbuddhyā kṛtvā pṛthaktataḥ // GkT_1.7:97
children.translated_text: afterwards one should meditate on Him alone, having separated [Him from attributes] through the intellect.

children.text: * ityetat pāśupatayogavidhānaṃ paramottamaṃ surairapi alabhyaṃ paramaguhyam ā parameśvarād gurupāramparyopadeśaikasamadhigamyaṃ svalpaprajñānām anugrahārthaṃ vyaktam evopanyastam // GkT_1.7:98
children.translated_text: Thus this supreme and most excellent <s>Pāśupata</s> <s>yoga</s> procedure, unobtainable even by the gods, supremely secret, comprehensible only through the lineage of teacher-to-teacher instruction from <s>Parameśvara</s> [Himself], has been clearly set forth for the sake of benefiting those of limited understanding.
