children.text: * yastvevaṃ na śraddadhātyaparīkṣitebhyo vā dadāti tasya brahmahatyādibhyo 'pi garīyaḥ pātakaṃ syād ityataḥ śiṣyaparīkṣāyāṃ śraddhāyāṃ ca yatnaḥ kartavya iti // GkT_1.7:99
children.translated_text: But one who does not have faith in this, or who imparts it to those who have not been examined — his sin would be graver even than the killing of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like. Therefore, effort must be made in the examination of the disciple and in [cultivating] faith.

children.text: * sthiter upāyamāha // GkT_1.7:100
children.translated_text: He states the means to <s>sthiti</s> (steadfastness):

children.text: * sadārudrasmṛtis tathā iti // GkT_1.7:101
children.translated_text: 'Constant remembrance of <s>Rudra</s>, likewise.'

children.text: * devanityatvameva sadāsmṛtir ity ucyate // GkT_1.7:102
children.translated_text: <s>Devanityatva</s> (constant devotion to God) itself is what is called 'constant remembrance.'

children.text: * sthitiṃ pratyupāyatvapratipādanārthaṃ saṃjñāntarābhidhānam iti // GkT_1.7:103
children.translated_text: The designation by another name is for the purpose of establishing its status as a means to <s>sthiti</s> (steadfastness).

children.text: * tathāśabdaḥ samānārthaḥ // GkT_1.7:104
children.translated_text: The word 'tathā' (likewise) has the same meaning [as before].

children.text: * yathā devanityatvaṃ pratyadhyayanadhyānayorevopāyatvaṃ dharmaṃ ca prati caryāyā eva tadanugrāhakatvenānusnānādiyamayantraṇādir apyupāyatvam upacaryate tathā sthitiṃ prati smṛtireva prādhānyenopāyas tadanugrāhakatvenendriyajayo 'pyupāyatvenokta ityato nendriyajayād ityanena virodhaḥ // GkT_1.7:105
children.translated_text: Just as <s>devanityatva</s> (constant devotion to God) serves as the [primary] means specifically for study and meditation, and with respect to <s>dharma</s> (religious observance) the <s>caryā</s> (conduct) alone [is the primary means], yet the subsidiary bath and other restraints are also figuratively called means because they support it — so too, with respect to <s>sthiti</s> (steadfastness), <s>smṛti</s> (remembrance) alone is the primary means, while the five means also support it.

children.text: * saṅgādinivṛtterupāyāntaramindriyajaya ityeke // GkT_1.7:106
children.translated_text: Some say: 'Mastery over the senses is an additional means for the cessation of attachment and the like.'

children.text: * tanna pañcopāyatvavirodhāt tyāgādānasūtrabhāṣyavirodhāc ca // GkT_1.7:107
children.translated_text: That is not so, because it contradicts the [doctrine of] five means, and because it contradicts the <s>Sūtra</s> and <s>Bhāṣya</s> [passages] on renunciation and acceptance.

children.text: * devanityatvendriyajayayor abheda ityanye 'pi // GkT_1.7:108
children.translated_text: Others also [say]: '<s>Devanityatva</s> (constant devotion to God) and mastery over the senses are non-different.'

children.text: * tadapi na // GkT_1.7:109
children.translated_text: That also is not [correct].

children.text: * lakṣaṇabhedādīndriyotsargagrahayoḥ prabhutvamindriyajayaḥ // GkT_1.7:110
children.translated_text: Because of the difference in definition — mastery over the senses is sovereignty over both the release and restraint of the senses.

children.text: * deve bhāvābhyāsataratvaṃ devanityatvamiti // GkT_1.7:111
children.translated_text: <s>Devanityatva</s> (constant devotion to God) is the intensity of repeated meditation on the God.

children.text: * siddhestarhyupāyo vācya ityata āha // GkT_1.7:112
children.translated_text: [Objection:] 'Then the means to <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) should be stated.' Therefore he says:

children.text: * prasādaś caiva iti // GkT_1.7:113
children.translated_text: 'And <s>prasāda</s> (grace) indeed.'

children.text: * kāraṇasya svaguṇaditsā prasāda ityucyate // GkT_1.7:114
children.translated_text: The desire of the Cause (God) to bestow His own qualities is called <s>prasāda</s> (grace).

children.text: * caśabdo nyūnādhikavyavacchedasūcakaḥ // GkT_1.7:115
children.translated_text: The word 'ca' (and) indicates the exclusion of anything less or more [than what is stated].

children.text: * evaśabdaḥ prasādasyānyānapekṣatvam avadhārayati // GkT_1.7:116
children.translated_text: The word 'eva' (indeed) determines that <s>prasāda</s> (grace) is independent of anything else.

children.text: * lābhānāmupāyā ityetad gamyamānārthasyāpyabhidhānaṃ śāstrāntaroktānāṃ mokṣopāyānām anupāyatvajñāpanārtham // GkT_1.7:117
children.translated_text: The statement 'these are the means to the attainments' — even though its meaning is already understood — is [made explicitly] for the purpose of making known that the means to liberation taught in other treatises are not [true] means.

children.text: * pañca ityupasaṃhārārtham // GkT_1.7:118
children.translated_text: 'Five' is for the purpose of summation.

children.text: * niścitā ityāptairdṛṣṭā ityarthaḥ // GkT_1.7:119
children.translated_text: 'Established' means 'perceived by authoritative persons.'

children.text: * atha kimetairupāyaiḥ pañcalābhā eva prāptavyā iti na kiṃ tarhi malāśca pañca kṣapaṇīyāḥ // GkT_1.7:120
children.translated_text: Now, [one may ask:] 'Are only the five attainments to be obtained by these means?' No; rather, five impurities (<s>mala</s>) are also to be destroyed.

children.text: * ke punaste ityāha // GkT_1.7:121]
children.translated_text: 'What then are they?' He says:

body.translated_text: [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: mithyājñānamadharmaśca saktihetuś cyutistathā /
children.translated_text: False knowledge, demerit, the cause of attachment, fall, likewise,

children.text: paśutvaṃ mūlaṃ pañcaite tantre heyādhikārataḥ // Gk_1.8
children.translated_text: and animality, the root — these five are to be abandoned according to the authority of the <s>Tantra</s>.

body.text: * [<Gaṇakārikāṭīkā>

children.text: * tatra pramāṇābhāsajaṃ jñānaṃ mithyājñānam uktaṃ saṃśayaviparyayādilakṣaṇam // GkT_1.8:1
children.translated_text: Among these, knowledge born from semblances of valid means of cognition is called <s>mithyājñāna</s> (false knowledge), characterized by doubt, error, and the like.

children.text: * śāstrāntarebhyo'pi tarhi saṃśayādinivṛtter aviśeṣaprasaṅga iti cen na śāstrāntarapraṇetḥṇām api viparyayānivṛttipratipādanād ācāryavaiśeṣyaprakaraṇe // GkT_1.8:2
children.translated_text: If [one objects:] 'Then there would be no distinction, since the cessation of doubt and the like can also [be obtained] from other treatises' — no, because the authors of other treatises also teach the non-cessation of error, [as discussed] in the section on the distinction of the <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher).

children.text: * tanna śāstrāntarebhyo'pi saṃśayādinivṛttiriti // GkT_1.8:3
children.translated_text: Therefore, the cessation of doubt and the like does not [occur] even from other treatises.

children.text: * kāmakrodhadveṣāḥ kaluṣaṃ tasyāpyajñāne 'ntarbhāvaḥ // GkT_1.8:4
children.translated_text: Desire, anger, and hatred are <s>kaluṣa</s> (impurity); this too is included within ignorance.

children.text: * kasmāt // GkT_1.8:5
children.translated_text: Why?

children.text: * avyaktāvasthāgamane pratyanīkatvāt // GkT_1.8:6
children.translated_text: Because it is opposed to the attainment of the unmanifest state.

children.text: * tadidaṃ saṃśayādi kaluṣaṃ ca saha bījena mithyājñānam ityucyate // GkT_1.8:7
children.translated_text: This — doubt and the like, together with impurity and its seed — is called <s>mithyājñāna</s> (false knowledge).

children.text: * dvitīyaṃ malaṃ darśayati adharmaśca iti // GkT_1.8:8
children.translated_text: He shows the second impurity: 'and <s>adharma</s> (demerit).'

children.text: * pāpmabījaṃ pāpam evātrādharma ityabhipretam // GkT_1.8:9
children.translated_text: What is meant here by <s>adharma</s> is sin itself, together with the seed of sin.

children.text: * tasya savikārasyaikamalatvaṃ vikāravikāriṇorananyatvād iti // GkT_1.8:10
children.translated_text: Its being a single impurity together with its modifications is because a modification and its source are non-different.

children.text: * saty apy ajñānakaluṣasaṅgacyutihetor adharmatve pāpākhya evātrādharmo 'bhipreta iti caḥ sūcayati // GkT_1.8:11
children.translated_text: The word 'ca' (and) indicates that although ignorance, impurity, attachment, and fall are also causes of <s>adharma</s>, what is meant here by <s>adharma</s> is specifically that which is called sin.

children.text: * tṛtīyaṃ malam āha // GkT_1.8:12
children.translated_text: He states the third impurity:

children.text: * saktihetuḥ iti // GkT_1.8:13
children.translated_text: '<s>Saktihetu</s>' (the cause of attachment).

children.text: * saktiḥ saṅgaḥ viṣayāsaktilakṣaṇasukhaṃ bhāṣye sukhābhimāna ityanenoktam // GkT_1.8:14
children.translated_text: <s>Sakti</s> (attachment) is <s>saṅga</s> (clinging); it is pleasure characterized by attachment to sense objects. In the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, it is expressed by the term '<s>sukhābhimāna</s>' (conceit of happiness).

children.text: * tasyaiva lakṣaṇārthaṃ bhāṣyam avivecanamiśraṇapreraṇalakṣaṇo vanagajavat iti // GkT_1.8:15
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhāṣya</s> defines its nature thus: 'It has the character of non-discrimination, intermixture, and impulsion, like a wild elephant.'

children.text: * tasya saṅgasya hetus tanmayakaraṇaṃ vidhyantaropārjito dharmaḥ saṅgakara iti ya uktaḥ saha vikāreṇāsau tṛtīyo mala iti // GkT_1.8:16
children.translated_text: The cause of that <s>saṅga</s> (attachment) is that which produces identification with it — the <s>dharma</s> (merit) acquired through other ritual injunctions that has been called 'attachment-producing.' Together with its modifications, this is the third impurity.

children.text: * caturthaṃ malam āha // GkT_1.8:17
children.translated_text: He states the fourth impurity:

children.text: * cyutis tathā iti // GkT_1.8:18
children.translated_text: '<s>Cyuti</s> (fall), likewise.'

children.text: * rudratattvādīṣaccittaṃ cyavate viṣayaṃ na prāpnoti taccittacyavanaṃ cyutir ityucyate // GkT_1.8:19
children.translated_text: When the mind, [directed] toward the <s>Rudra</s>-reality and the like, lapses slightly and does not attain [its] object — that lapsing of the mind is called <s>cyuti</s> (fall).

children.text: * tathāśabdaḥ samānārthe // GkT_1.8:20
children.translated_text: The word 'tathā' (likewise) has the same meaning [as before].

children.text: * yathā mithyājñānasya svabījena saha malatvam adharmasaṅgakarayoś ca savikāreṇa tathā cyuterapi ūṣmavad avasthitādharmākhyena svabījena saha malatvam iti // GkT_1.8:21
children.translated_text: Just as <s>mithyājñāna</s> (false knowledge) together with its own seed constitutes an impurity, and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) and the attachment-cause together with their modifications [constitute impurities], so too <s>cyuti</s> (fall) together with its own seed — called <s>adharma</s> that remains latent like heat — constitutes an impurity.

children.text: * atra bhāṣyavirodhānna mithyājñānakaluṣapāpmasaṅgacyutayaḥ puruṣasya bhāvāś cittavidyayor vā // GkT_1.8:22
children.translated_text: Here, because of [the statements in] the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, false knowledge, impurity, sin, attachment, and fall are not properties of the <s>puruṣa</s> (self), nor of the mind or knowledge.

children.text: * nāpi kaluṣamicchāyā bhāvaḥ kiṃtvadharmavikārā evaite jñānecchābhyāṃ saha kṣīrodakavad abhinnā iva gṛhyante // GkT_1.8:23
children.translated_text: Nor is impurity a property of desire; rather, these are all modifications of <s>adharma</s> (demerit) that are apprehended as though inseparable from knowledge and desire, like milk and water.

children.text: * tathā ca satkāryavicāre prapañcitametad iti // GkT_1.8:24
children.translated_text: And this has been elaborated in the examination of the <s>satkārya</s> [doctrine] (the doctrine that the effect pre-exists in the cause).

children.text: * pañcamaṃ malamāha paśutvam iti // GkT_1.8:25
children.translated_text: He states the fifth impurity: '<s>paśutva</s> (animality).'

children.text: * dharmādharmavyatiriktaḥ pratighātānumeyaḥ puruṣaguṇaḥ paśutvam // GkT_1.8:26
children.translated_text: <s>Paśutva</s> (animality) is a quality of the <s>puruṣa</s> (self) that is distinct from <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), and is inferred from [the experience of] obstruction.

children.text: * tasya caturdaśalakṣaṇopetasya malatvam // GkT_1.8:27
children.translated_text: Its being an impurity is [established by] its possessing fourteen characteristics.

children.text: * tāni ca lakṣaṇāny asarvajñatvādīny apatitvāntāni sarvajñatvādiviparyayeṇaiva vyākhyātānīti // GkT_1.8:28
children.translated_text: And those characteristics — beginning with non-omniscience and ending with non-lordship — are explained simply as the opposites of omniscience and the like.

children.text: * taccetthaṃbhūtaṃ paśutvaṃ saṃsārasyānādikāraṇaṃ pradhānabhūtam ityevaṃ matvāha mūlamiti // GkT_1.8:29
children.translated_text: Considering that <s>paśutva</s> (animality) of this nature is the beginningless and principal cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, he says '<s>mūla</s>' (the root).

children.text: * tathāhi kaivalyagatānāmanyamalābhāve 'pi paśutvādeva punaḥ saṃsārāpattiriti // GkT_1.8:30
children.translated_text: For indeed, even for those who have attained <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), when the other impurities are absent, it is from <s>paśutva</s> (animality) alone that there is return to <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: * pañca iti nyūnādhikavyavacchedenopasaṃhārārtham // GkT_1.8:31
children.translated_text: 'Five' is for the purpose of summation by excluding anything less or more.

children.text: * ete ityavadhāraṇārtham // GkT_1.8:32
children.translated_text: 'These' is for the purpose of determination.

children.text: * ete eva saṃsārabandhātmakā malā na tu śāstrāntaroktā bhoktṛbhogyasambandhādaya ityarthaḥ // GkT_1.8:33
children.translated_text: The meaning is: these alone are the impurities constituting the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>, not those spoken of in other treatises such as the relation of experiencer and experienced, and the like.

children.text: * kva punaritthaṃbhūtā malāḥ prasiddhā ityāha // GkT_1.8:34
children.translated_text: 'Where then are such impurities taught?' He says:

children.text: * tantre sākṣān maheśvarapraṇītam athaśabdādi śivāntaṃ śāstraṃ tantraṃ tasminnete pratipāditā ityarthaḥ // GkT_1.8:35
children.translated_text: 'In the <s>Tantra</s>' — the treatise directly composed by <s>Maheśvara</s>, beginning with the word 'atha' and ending with '<s>Śiva</s>' — that is the <s>Tantra</s>. The meaning is: these [impurities] are set forth therein.

children.text: * dharmajñānāderapi tyajyamānatvād adharmāderiva malatvaṃ prāptamityāśaṅkyāha heyādhikārataḥ iti // GkT_1.8:36
children.translated_text: Anticipating the objection that since <s>dharma</s> (merit), knowledge, and the like are also to be abandoned, they too would have the status of impurities just like <s>adharma</s> and the like, he says: '<s>heyādhikārataḥ</s>' (according to the authority [of the <s>Tantra</s>] regarding what is to be abandoned).

children.text: * yeṣāṃ kardamādivadduḥkhahetutvaṃ matvā sādhakaḥ kṣapaṇārtham adhikriyate ta eva malā na tu yeṣāṃ puṣpādivadanicchato'pi vināśa ityato heyādhikārād ajñānādaya eva malā iti // GkT_1.8:37
children.translated_text: * Those which, having understood them to be causes of suffering like mud etc., the practitioner undertakes to eradicate — those alone are impurities (<s>mala</s>), not those which are destroyed even without one's wish, like flowers etc. Therefore, from the scope of what is to be abandoned (<s>heya</s>), ignorance and the rest alone are the impurities. // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:37

children.text: * heyādhikārikā iti vā pāṭhastatrāpyayam arthaḥ // GkT_1.8:38
children.translated_text: * Or the reading is '<s>heyādhikārikā</s>'; in that case too, this is the meaning: // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:38

children.text: * heyatvena kṣapaṇīyatvenādhikāro yogyatāsti yeṣāṃ te heyādhikāriṇasta eva heyādhikārikāḥ // GkT_1.8:39
children.translated_text: * Those which have eligibility (<s>yogyatā</s>) for being abandoned, i.e., for being eradicated — they are <s>heyādhikāriṇas</s>; those very ones are <s>heyādhikārikāḥ</s>. // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:39

children.text: * svārthe kapratyayaḥ // GkT_1.8:40
children.translated_text: * The suffix 'ka' is in the reflexive sense (<s>svārthe</s>). // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:40

children.text: * adhikāraśabdād vā ikaṅpratyaye kṛte heyapadena karmadhārayas tadayamartho yato heyādhikārikā evātra malā vivakṣitāḥ // GkT_1.8:41
children.translated_text: * Or, when the suffix '<s>ikan</s>' is applied to the word '<s>adhikāra</s>,' a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound is formed with the word '<s>heya</s>' — this is the meaning: since only the impurities that are <s>heyādhikārikā</s> (subject to abandonment) are intended here. // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:41

children.text: * tasmānna dharmajñānavairāgyādayo'pi malā iti // GkT_1.8:42
children.translated_text: * Therefore, <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and the like are not impurities. // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:42

children.text: * ityetatsarvamākhyātaṃ saṃkṣipyābdhisamaṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: * Thus all this has been stated by me in summary, [vast] as the ocean,

children.text: * ācāryāṇāṃ prasādena jñānaṃ pañcārthalakṣaṇam // GkT_1.8:43
children.translated_text: * by the grace of the teachers — the knowledge characterized by the five categories (<s>pañcārtha</s>). // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:43

children.text: * kiṃ jñātairbahubhiḥ śāstraiḥ svānuṣṭhānāpahāribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: * What use are many scriptures that rob one of one's own practice?

children.text: * idamevottamaṃ jñātvā yogābhyāsaratirbhavet // GkT_1.8:44
children.translated_text: * Having known this alone as supreme, one should delight in the practice of <s>yoga</s>. // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:44

children.text: * kṛtakṛtyaṃ svamātmānaṃ śrutvaitanmanyate tu yaḥ /
children.translated_text: * He who, having heard this, considers himself to have accomplished his purpose —

children.text: * tasmai deyamidaṃ jñānaṃ nānyasmin siddhimicchatā // GkT_1.8:45
children.translated_text: * to him should this knowledge be given; one desiring <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) should not [give it] to any other. // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:45

children.text: * yastu maryādāhīnebhyo dadyātkenāpi hetunā /
children.translated_text: * But he who would give [this knowledge] to those lacking proper boundaries, for whatever reason,

children.text: * sa guhyabhedato gacchetsaha śiṣyairadhogatim // GkT_1.8:46
children.translated_text: * he, due to the breach of secrecy, shall go to a low destination together with his disciples. // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:46

children.text: * namaḥ sadgurave tasmai sarvavidyāntagāmine /
children.translated_text: * Homage to that true teacher (<s>sadguru</s>), who has reached the end of all knowledge,

children.text: * sacchlokair aṣṭabhir yena pañcārthābdhiḥ pradarśitaḥ // GkT_1.8:47]
children.translated_text: * by whom, through eight excellent verses, the ocean of the <s>Pañcārtha</s> (five categories) has been revealed. // <s>GkT</s> 1.8:47]
